screenings.title: Visible Humans
screenings.description: With artist and ophthalmologist Benjamin Freeman and curator Elisabeth Sherman in person The Visible Human Project began in the late 1990s with sponsorship from the National Library of Medicine. Its aim was to make a complete 3D rendering of the human body for educational use. Now in the public domain, these images raise questions about consent and normative ideals. This evening will interrogate this project and feature a screening of the short film Visible Woman, which is included in our exhibition Overexposed; a presentation by ophthalmologist and photographer Benjamin Freeman; and a discussion including curator Elisabeth Sherman. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. Special Guests: Elisabeth Sherman is the Robert A. and Elizabeth Rohn Jeffe Chief Curator and Deputy Director at the Museum of the City of New York. Previously, she was Chief Curator and Director of Curatorial Affairs at the International Center of Photography (ICP). Prior to ICP, she was a curator at the Whitney Museum of American Art, where she organized and co-organized many critically acclaimed exhibitions including Dawoud Bey: An American Project, Zoe Leonard: Survey, and Making Knowing: Craft in Art, 1960-2019. At ICP she curated, among others, Naima Green: Instead, I Spin Fantasies, Sheida Soleimani: Panjereh, Yto Barrada: Part Time Abstractionist, and ICP at 50. She is co-editor of the catalog Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body. Benji Freeman is a photographer and physician based in New York City. His photography draws from medical epistemologies, techniques, and image archives, investigating the modern aesthetics of caring for others as the actual work of healthcare becomes increasingly automatable. He has taught workshops on photographic technique, the visual culture of medicine, and the anatomy of the visual system, and he has written about the role of photographic perception in medical education. He is currently an ophthalmology resident at Columbia University Medical Center.

THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. screenings.title: Club Kid

screenings.title: La Bola Negra
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Birds of War
screenings.description: Spanning 13 years of revolution, war and exile, from besieged Aleppo to the confines of a London newsroom, Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian activist and cameraman Abd Alkader Habak relive their war reporting and their unexpected love story, using a vast personal trove of archives.

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Avedon
screenings.description: AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used photography to reinvent the world around him. Drawing on unprecedented access to his personal archives—never-before-seen stills, intimate behind-the-lens footage, and new interviews with his closest collaborators—the film explores how his singular eye both reflected and reshaped the visual language of the 20th century, and why even the most iconic image is only half the story.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.description: Hen chronicles a remarkable chicken as she escapes her grisly fate in this unorthodox and bold story from director György Pálfi, telling a tall tale of human misery via a small bird in search of home. In Greek with English subtitles.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
Fjord
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine
screenings.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass
Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Mouse
screenings.description: It’s 2002, and best friends Minnie and Callie are heading into their senior year of high school, with Minnie long living in the protective shadow of the charismatic and admired Callie. When their friendship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer, Minnie struggles to define her own identity and forms a complicated relationship with Callie’s poised, attentive mother, pulling her further from her own chaotic home.

screenings.title: The Cat in the Hat
screenings.description: Followed by a Q&A with production designer Aidan Sugano Dirs. Erica Rivinoja, Alessandro Carloni. 2026.107 min. U.S. DCP. With Bill Hader, Matt Berry, Quinta Brunson, Xochitl Gomez, Tiago Martinez, Giancarlo Esposito, America Ferrera, Bowen Yang. Meet the Cat in the Hat you don’t know! In the wonderfully whimsical tradition of Dr. Seuss, The Cat in the Hat, voiced by Bill Hader, comes to the big screen in his animated theatrical feature film debut, an all-new, epic adventure where mischief, magic and mayhem reign supreme. Doing what he does best, the Cat—voiced by Bill Hader—spreads joy to kids in his hilarious, signature and singularly irreverent way, transporting them and audiences on a fantastical journey through a world they’ve never seen before. In the film, our hero takes on his toughest assignment yet for the I.I.I.I. (Institute for the Institution of Imagination and Inspiration, LLC): to cheer Gabby and Sebastian, a pair of siblings struggling with their move to a new town. Known for taking things too far, this could be this agent of chaos’s last chance to prove himself…or lose his magical hat! A Warner Brothers Animation release, in theaters November 6, 2026. Watch the trailer here. Free with RSVP. Limited capacity.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Tech founder Elizabeth Holmes invites Nathan Fielder to film her before she’s sent to prison.

screenings.title: Spellbound
screenings.description: Hitchcock goes in for psychoanalysis in this singular thriller, made under the influence of Sigmund Freud and Salvador Dalí, the latter of whom designed the dazzling dream sequence. Analyst Ingrid Bergman falls for amnesiac patient Gregory Peck—but is there a murderer’s heart lurking beneath that dapper exterior? The delirium only grows more intense and Miklós Rózsa’s theremin-inflected score becomes more urgent as her doubts grow and she draws closer to the truth.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Far From Heaven
screenings.description: An homage to the Eisenhower era melodramas of Douglas Sirk that reworks the basic materials of his 1955 All That Heaven Allows to explicitly explore dynamics of sexual and social transgression verboten in the Hollywood of Sirk’s time, Haynes’s sumptuous film—featuring a period-appropriate score by Elmer Bernstein and a remarkable approximation of Technicolor saturation by cinematographer Ed Lachman—stars Julianne Moore and Dennis Quaid as a well-heeled Connecticut couple whose seemingly perfect suburban existence is upended when he’s discovered trawling Hartford’s gay bars and she strikes up an affair with her new Black gardener, played with compassionate gravity by Dennis Haysbert.

screenings.title: Leonora in the Morning Light + Q&A
screenings.description: In the early 1930s, painter Leonora Carrington, a rebel against social expectations, joins the surrealist movement and its iconic figures like André Breton and Salvador Dalí in Paris. A whirlwind love affair with artist Max Ernst confronts her with her inner demons. During the war, Leonora flees to Mexico and finally empowers herself. Today Leonora Carrington is one of the highest selling female painters worldwide, next to Frida Kahlo and Georgia O’Keeffe.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.description: See the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience Ken Russell envisioned for his 1971 classic.

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: The Correspondent
screenings.description: Award-winning journalist Peter Greste reports on the Arab Spring uprising, becoming entangled in a deadly game of rivalries. Imprisoned for seven years despite his innocence, he survives on wits alone before release in 2015.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: The writer Thomas Mann and his daughter embark on a road trip across a divided Germany.

screenings.title: The Hard Part Begins
screenings.description: If fans of previous Spectacle classic Payday are looking for another downbeat 1973 road movie by a Canadian director about a deeply toxic country singer, they should look no further than The Hard Part Begins. Donnelly Rhodes inhabits King with a mixture of charm and bitterness that befits the character’s big-fish small-pond aspirations, while future Prom Night director Paul Lynch finds a ramshackle beauty in its world of van journeys and dive bars. The Hard Part Begins presages Inside Llewyn Davis in its balance of an unforgiving portrait of its protagonist with a sympathy for the also-rans following their artistic ambitions to the bitter end.

screenings.title: 5 Short Films Supported by the Displacement Film Fund
screenings.description: Actor and producer Cate Blanchett, together with International Film Festival Rotterdam’s (IFFR) Hubert Bals Fund, will host the New York premiere of the Displacement Film Fund’s inaugural slate of films on November 11 at Film Forum. Co-founded and led by Blanchett, the Displacement Film Fund (DFF) was established to champion and fund the work of displaced filmmakers, or filmmakers with a proven track record in creating authentic stories focused on the experiences of displaced people. Timely, surprising and intimate, the shorts in this critically acclaimed collection are directed by internationally renowned filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine), Mo Harawe (Somalia-Austria), Hasan Kattan (Syria), Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran), and Shahrbanoo Sadat (Afghanistan). All five films will be presented at Film Forum, with filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach and Mo Harawe in person at each program. After premiering at the 2026 International Film Festival Rotterdam, this collection was invited to the London, Sao Paulo (Mostra), and Tokyo international film festivals. The films will be released on The New Yorker this November. Rotation dir. Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine, Turkey) 12 min. Rotation is a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who shifted from civilian life to military service. She needs support to adapt to the displaced reality she now lives in. Gorbach’s KLONDIKE was Winner of the World Cinema Dramatic Directing Award at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival. Super Afghan Gym dir. Shahrbanoo Sadat (Germany) 14 min. In a gym in downtown Kabul, a group of housewives gather during the only hour of the day reserved for women. They train at lunchtime behind closed doors, talking about body norms and their daily life. Sadat’s most recent film, NO GOOD MEN, was the opening night selection of the 2026 Berlin Film Festival. Allies in Exile dir. Hasan Kattan (United Kingdom) 40 min. For 14 years, Syrian filmmakers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi have journeyed together through war and storytelling. Confined inside a UK asylum hotel, Hasan and Fadi document a new chapter shaped not by bombs, but by waiting, bureaucracy, and exile. Amid rising anti-refugee hostility, they turn the camera inward exploring friendship and displacement and how filming itself becomes an act of survival when the future is so uncertain. Kattan served as cinematographer on the Oscar®-winning The White Helmets and assistant director on the Oscar®-nominated LAST MEN IN ALEPPO. Whispers of a Burning Scent dir. Mo Harawe (Somalia, Austria, Germany) 27 min. On the day of a decisive court hearing and an important wedding performance, a quiet wedding musician finds his private life exposed to public scrutiny. Accused of exploiting his marriage, he moves between courtroom, city streets and stage, carrying the weight of judgment, loyalty, and unspoken guilt. Forced to make a restrained but irreversible decision, the film observes a man whose inner truth remains elusive, caught between devotion, dignity, and loss. Harawe’s feature debut, THE VILLAGE NEXT TO PARADISE, was the first Somali film featured as an official selection of the Cannes Film Festival, where it had its world premiere in 2024. Sense of Water dir. Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran, Germany) 39 min. In the chill of exile, an Iranian writer confronts a foreign language—a language in which he must rediscover love, anger, joy, and sorrow in order to write again. His quest to reclaim the power of writing becomes an inner journey between memory and forgetting, between a lost language and a new one, where human emotion and meaning must be recreated anew. Rasoulof directed THE SEED OF THE SACRED FIG (Special Jury Prize winner at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival) and THERE IS NO EVIL (Golden Bear winner at the 2020 Berlin Film Festival), both Film Forum U.S. theatrical premieres. ---------------------------------- With one in every 70 people on earth forcibly displaced due to conflict, war, or persecution, the global community is witnessing an unprecedented crisis. The Displacement Film Fund was first conceived at the 2023 Global Refugee Forum, hosted by UNHCR and the world’s largest gathering dedicated to addressing challenges faced by refugees and their host communities. Blanchett joined forces with a group of film industry experts and creatives, all of whom have a personal connection and/or strong interest in the issue of forced displacement—and established the Fund—which launched at IFFR 2025—with a mission of giving visibility and bringing to the mainstream stories of displacement, while highlighting the diversity of displacement-related life experiences. IFFR’s Hubert Bals Fund is the Management Partner and it was founded in partnership with the Amahoro Coalition, MASTERMIND, the Tamer Family Foundation, UNIQLO and Droom en Daad. In 2026, the SP Lohia Foundation joined as Main Partner. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency act as Strategic Partner.

screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1971. 137 mins. 35mm. With Malcolm McDowell, Patrick Magee, Adrienne Corri, Miriam Carlin. Stanley Kubrick’s savage adaptation of Anthony Burgess’s 1962 novel is among the most infamous and controversial mainstream movies ever made. McDowell is unforgettable as Alex, the amoral, nihilist, Beethoven-obsessed head of the Droogs, a gang of marauding teen rapists and murderers rampaging across a dystopic, diseased future London. After arrest, he is subject to a treatment in which his violent impulses are turned back on him, leading to provocative questions about government control and free will. A Clockwork Orange, which was rated X upon release, remains shocking, bleak, and grimly funny. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. screenings.title: Avedon
screenings.description: AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used photography to reinvent the world around him. Drawing on unprecedented access to his personal archives—never-before-seen stills, intimate behind-the-lens footage, and new interviews with his closest collaborators—the film explores how his singular eye both reflected and reshaped the visual language of the 20th century, and why even the most iconic image is only half the story.

screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: 5 Short Films Supported by the Displacement Film Fund
screenings.description: Actor and producer Cate Blanchett, together with International Film Festival Rotterdam’s (IFFR) Hubert Bals Fund, will host the New York premiere of the Displacement Film Fund’s inaugural slate of films on November 11 at Film Forum. Co-founded and led by Blanchett, the Displacement Film Fund (DFF) was established to champion and fund the work of displaced filmmakers, or filmmakers with a proven track record in creating authentic stories focused on the experiences of displaced people. Timely, surprising and intimate, the shorts in this critically acclaimed collection are directed by internationally renowned filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine), Mo Harawe (Somalia-Austria), Hasan Kattan (Syria), Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran), and Shahrbanoo Sadat (Afghanistan). All five films will be presented at Film Forum, with filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach and Mo Harawe in person at each program. After premiering at the 2026 International Film Festival Rotterdam, this collection was invited to the London, Sao Paulo (Mostra), and Tokyo international film festivals. The films will be released on The New Yorker this November. Rotation dir. Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine, Turkey) 12 min. Rotation is a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who shifted from civilian life to military service. She needs support to adapt to the displaced reality she now lives in. Gorbach’s KLONDIKE was Winner of the World Cinema Dramatic Directing Award at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival. Super Afghan Gym dir. Shahrbanoo Sadat (Germany) 14 min. In a gym in downtown Kabul, a group of housewives gather during the only hour of the day reserved for women. They train at lunchtime behind closed doors, talking about body norms and their daily life. Sadat’s most recent film, NO GOOD MEN, was the opening night selection of the 2026 Berlin Film Festival. Allies in Exile dir. Hasan Kattan (United Kingdom) 40 min. For 14 years, Syrian filmmakers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi have journeyed together through war and storytelling. Confined inside a UK asylum hotel, Hasan and Fadi document a new chapter shaped not by bombs, but by waiting, bureaucracy, and exile. Amid rising anti-refugee hostility, they turn the camera inward exploring friendship and displacement and how filming itself becomes an act of survival when the future is so uncertain. Kattan served as cinematographer on the Oscar®-winning The White Helmets and assistant director on the Oscar®-nominated LAST MEN IN ALEPPO. Whispers of a Burning Scent dir. Mo Harawe (Somalia, Austria, Germany) 27 min. On the day of a decisive court hearing and an important wedding performance, a quiet wedding musician finds his private life exposed to public scrutiny. Accused of exploiting his marriage, he moves between courtroom, city streets and stage, carrying the weight of judgment, loyalty, and unspoken guilt. Forced to make a restrained but irreversible decision, the film observes a man whose inner truth remains elusive, caught between devotion, dignity, and loss. Harawe’s feature debut, THE VILLAGE NEXT TO PARADISE, was the first Somali film featured as an official selection of the Cannes Film Festival, where it had its world premiere in 2024. Sense of Water dir. Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran, Germany) 39 min. In the chill of exile, an Iranian writer confronts a foreign language—a language in which he must rediscover love, anger, joy, and sorrow in order to write again. His quest to reclaim the power of writing becomes an inner journey between memory and forgetting, between a lost language and a new one, where human emotion and meaning must be recreated anew. Rasoulof directed THE SEED OF THE SACRED FIG (Special Jury Prize winner at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival) and THERE IS NO EVIL (Golden Bear winner at the 2020 Berlin Film Festival), both Film Forum U.S. theatrical premieres. ---------------------------------- With one in every 70 people on earth forcibly displaced due to conflict, war, or persecution, the global community is witnessing an unprecedented crisis. The Displacement Film Fund was first conceived at the 2023 Global Refugee Forum, hosted by UNHCR and the world’s largest gathering dedicated to addressing challenges faced by refugees and their host communities. Blanchett joined forces with a group of film industry experts and creatives, all of whom have a personal connection and/or strong interest in the issue of forced displacement—and established the Fund—which launched at IFFR 2025—with a mission of giving visibility and bringing to the mainstream stories of displacement, while highlighting the diversity of displacement-related life experiences. IFFR’s Hubert Bals Fund is the Management Partner and it was founded in partnership with the Amahoro Coalition, MASTERMIND, the Tamer Family Foundation, UNIQLO and Droom en Daad. In 2026, the SP Lohia Foundation joined as Main Partner. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency act as Strategic Partner.

screenings.title: Last Stop for the Circular Ticket
screenings.description: THE THEATER OF THE MATTERS & TAUFIC PRESENT:JEAN-CLAUDE ROUSSEAU’S ‘THE PASTORAL CONCERT’ + ‘LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET’This book launch event celebrates the release of Jean-Claude Rousseau’s unclassifiable, long-unavailable film text, The Pastoral Concert, published for the first time in English this October by Taufic. The evening will culminate in a special premiere screening of Rousseau’s new feature film, LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET (winner of a Jury Special Mention at this year’s FIDMarseille), alongside his 2006 short, FAUX DÉPART.The Pastoral Concert marks the first English translation of Rousseau’s early written work Le Concert champêtre, begun in 1968, some fifteen years before his debut film. Rousseau continued shaping the work as a screenplay until its rejection by the Centre National de la Cinématographie in 1983. Unrealized, Le Concert champêtre became the matrix from which Rousseau’s subsequent films would emerge.Taking its title and three central characters (A, B, and C) from the eponymous painting long attributed to Giorgione and now to Titian, The Pastoral Concert begins as a letter written by a young man to his cousin in the countryside on the eve of her wedding, before mutating into a diary entry, a screenplay, and finally a film imagined through the failure of its own realization. In this restless fluctuation between registers, The Pastoral Concert expresses, in the words of Jean-Marie Straub, “something magnificent [and] entirely different from a screenplay or a découpage.”Translated from the French by artist and filmmaker Kevin Weil, this edition includes an extensive appendix of extra-diegetic materials written by Rousseau, as well as correspondence with contemporaries such as Dominique Noguez, Marcel Hanoun, and Jean-Marie Straub, which form a picture of the work’s early reception.For more info about The Pastoral Concert visit: https://taufic.org/the-pastoral-concertJean-Claude RousseauLAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET / DERNIER ARRÊT POUR LE BILLET CIRCULAIRE2026, 87 min, DCP. No dialogue.Rousseau’s longest film since THE ENCLOSED VALLEY from 1995 (the summit of his 8mm era), LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET refers to the looped ferry route that plies the waters of Lake Como in Northern Italy. Firmly grounded in place, Rousseau’s solitary camera finds desolate poetry in the void of the spectacular landscape and in the anonymous crowds of passengers seemingly entranced at the edge of an abyss. Musical chords and voices magnify their gestures and the movement of the vessel on the lake. Closing the circle, the specter of the end looms: “On the ferry, among the travelers, I recognized Mrs. Death…”Preceded by:Jean-Claude Rousseau FAUX DÉPART (2006, 13 min, DCP. screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.description: The follow-up to his Midnight Movie sensation El Topo, writer-director Alejandro Jodorowsky’s THE HOLY MOUNTAIN caused a scandal at the 1973 Cannes Film Festival with its flood of sacrilegious imagery, existential symbolism and outrageous violence. Once again, Jodorowsky plays the allegorically named lead, “The Alchemist,” who assembles a group of people from all walks of life and renames them for the planets in the solar system. Putting his recruits through strange mystical rites and divesting them of their worldly baggage, he leads them on a trip to Lotus Island to ascend the Holy Mountain and displace the immortal gods who secretly rule the universe. This gorgeous new digital restoration, overseen by the filmmaker himself, returns Jodorowsky’s most visually extravagant film to all its trippy splendor.

screenings.title: Flight to Hell
screenings.description: A garish amalgam of Westworld and The Mummy, Passeri’s 2000 masterpiece addresses the controversial practice of planting microchips in mummies in order to staff fantasy theme parks. Transcending its influences, the film boasts a uniquely queasy visual style crafted from greasy animatronics and a painfully saturated color palette. The plot concerns two dimwitted American journalists caught in the meltdown of the titular Mummy Theme Park – this, of course, is of secondary significance beside the exercise in discount worldmaking achieved through Passeri’s fabric-store scenography and a script rife with non-sequiturs.

screenings.title: The Reflecting Skin
screenings.description: Growing up in the 1950s in small-town Idaho, 8-year-old Seth and his friends play a prank on the town recluse, a mysterious English widow named Dolphin Blue (Tony winner Lindsay Duncan). After his father tells him stories of vampires, Seth becomes convinced Dolphin is a vampire, stealing the souls of his neighborhood friends one by one. When his older brother Cameron (Oscar nominee Viggo Mortensen in one of his first starring roles), returns home from military service in the Pacific and takes a liking to Dolphin, Seth feels it’s up to him to save Cameron from his friends’ fate. With stunning visuals recalling Edward Hopper paintings and its surreal blend of horror and humor, THE REFLECTING SKIN is a “stunningly beautiful…Gothic masterpiece” (The Guardian)!”

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine
screenings.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: The Devils
screenings.description: Ken Russell’s controversial adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun is at long last available in its full, provocative splendor. This new restoration thrillingly incorporates material that was originally censored—footage that Russell deemed some of the best and most political work of his career. A young Derek Jarman designed the sets that house this story of a vengeful nun (Vanessa Redgrave) who accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, resulting in the apparent possession of an entire convent. A fearless account of state and church corruption, The Devils mixes graphic sexual imagery with religious iconography in an unforgettable spectacle that could only issue from the mind of Ken Russell. Following its NYFF64 premiere, The Devils will open on 35mm for a one-week engagement beginning October 16 at Film at Lincoln Center. A Warner Bros. Clockwork release.

In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
screenings.description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

screenings.title: Club Kid in 35mm

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Far From Heaven
screenings.description: An homage to the Eisenhower era melodramas of Douglas Sirk that reworks the basic materials of his 1955 All That Heaven Allows to explicitly explore dynamics of sexual and social transgression verboten in the Hollywood of Sirk’s time, Haynes’s sumptuous film—featuring a period-appropriate score by Elmer Bernstein and a remarkable approximation of Technicolor saturation by cinematographer Ed Lachman—stars Julianne Moore and Dennis Quaid as a well-heeled Connecticut couple whose seemingly perfect suburban existence is upended when he’s discovered trawling Hartford’s gay bars and she strikes up an affair with her new Black gardener, played with compassionate gravity by Dennis Haysbert.

screenings.title: The Housemaid
screenings.description: Cited by Bong Joon-ho as an inspiration on his Parasite and widely regarded by South Korean cinephiles and scholars as one of the country’s greatest films, The Housemaid can now be discovered by the rest of the world thanks to a restoration by the Korean Film Archive and Martin Scorsese’s World Cinema Project. The routine domestic life of a middle-class family is turned upside-down after a young woman (Lee Eun-shim) joins the household to help with the chores—though what she does instead is turn the house into a boiling cauldron of lust. A mélange of melodrama, morality tale, noir thriller, and horror film that, in Kim’s handling, come together to exercise a vice-like grip.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Testament with Lynne Littman in person
screenings.description: Followed by a Q&A with director Lynne Littman Dir. Lynne Littman. 1983, 89 mins. U.S. 35mm print courtesy of the Lynne Littman Collection at the Academy Film Archive. With Jane Alexander, William Devane, Roxana Zal, Ross Harris, Lukas Haas, Leon Ames, Kevin Costner, Rebecca DeMornay. No one who has seen Testament has ever forgotten it. Released at the height of the Cold War nuclear scare of the early 1980s, this harrowing, intimate drama stars Jane Alexander, in an Oscar-nominated performance, as a California wife and mother struggling to hold her family together after the unthinkable happens: a nuclear strike on the U.S. Keeping the focus entirely on one household and the tight-knit neighborhood around it, director Lynne Littman fashioned the scariest and subtlest movie about the end of the world in American cinema history. We are pleased to present this underseen masterpiece with director Littman in person. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: Queen at Sea

Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem

A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.description: Based on two manga by Yoshiharu Tsuge, who rose to underground celebrity thanks to his surrealist tales published in the pages of Garo, the bastion of Japanese avant-garde cartooning, Miyake’s bifurcated live-action feature observes (and draws parallels and contrasts from) a summertime meet-cute between Nagisa and Natsuo (Yuumi Kawai and Mansaku Takada) and a snowbound winter encounter between screenwriter Li and innkeeper Ben-zō (Shim Eun-kyung and Shinichi Tsutsumi). Winner of the Golden Leopard at last year’s Locarno Film Festival, hailed “a true masterpiece” by Shiguéhiko Hasumi, Japan’s greatest living film critic, Two Seasons, Two Strangers is at one and the same time as simple as its straightforward title suggests and immensely, exhilaratingly complex. Preceded by Miyake’s short Nagahama, born of a creative collaboration with dancer and actress Shizuka Ishibashi.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol

Her 2023 narrative short Sulam (Ladder) premiered in competition at Aspen Shortsfest and won Best U.S. Student Film at Palm Springs ShortFest; her feature screenplay Princess won NYU’s Purple List Table-Read Initiative, where it was staged in its entirety for producers and executives; and her latest short, Verse, received the Sloan Production Award for its exploration of VR and neuroscience and had its world premiere at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival. Sappir starred in short films for top-tier MFA programs, including NYU Tisch and UCLA, as well as an independent short screened for producers at Blumhouse. She is also starring in two upcoming projects slated for release in 2026. Her commercial work includes a global travel campaign aired on NBC. In her writing, Sappir’s original podcast Passing Through ranked in the Top 100 narrative comedy shows on Apple Podcasts.

screenings.title: Personal Problems | The Ravishing Cinema of Bill Gunn
screenings.description: What happens when a group of unbankable individuals tell their stories? Actors who have final say over their speaking parts? A director who was found ‘too difficult’ for Hollywood? A composer who would not submit the hack soundtracks required by the industry? A Black male lead who was not Black enough? A Black actress who was not light enough? An actor who had been retired because he belonged to another era? A cinematographer who chose art over expediency? An unmarketable co-actor who didn’t look like Clark Gable or a male version of Vanessa Williams? Two producers, having no experience, had the audacity to organize a production with the amount of money that Hollywood spends on catering? Maybe less.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: Dir. John Schlesinger. 1969, 113 mins. U.S. 4K DCP. With Dustin Hoffman, Jon Voight, Sylvia Miles, Brenda Vaccaro. John Voight’s wannabe gigolo Joe Buck leaves Texas and winds up hustling on 42nd Street, bonding with the blighted block’s genius loci, Dustin Hoffman’s tubercular petty thief Ratzo Rizzo. Adapting a book by James Leo Herlihy, screenwriter Waldo Salt and British director John Schlesinger (in his first American film) fashioned something so brutally honest and daring that it became an instant sensation. Probably the most desperately romantic New York movie of its era, John Schlesinger’s astonishing, downtrodden Midnight Cowboy won three Oscars including Best Picture despite being the first major studio production released with an X. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Birds of War
screenings.description: Spanning 13 years of revolution, war and exile, from besieged Aleppo to the confines of a London newsroom, Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian activist and cameraman Abd Alkader Habak relive their war reporting and their unexpected love story, using a vast personal trove of archives.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: Avedon
screenings.description: AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used photography to reinvent the world around him. Drawing on unprecedented access to his personal archives—never-before-seen stills, intimate behind-the-lens footage, and new interviews with his closest collaborators—the film explores how his singular eye both reflected and reshaped the visual language of the 20th century, and why even the most iconic image is only half the story.

When their friendship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer, Minnie struggles to define her own identity and forms a complicated relationship with Callie’s poised, attentive mother, pulling her further from her own chaotic home.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.description: Hen chronicles a remarkable chicken as she escapes her grisly fate in this unorthodox and bold story from director György Pálfi, telling a tall tale of human misery via a small bird in search of home. In Greek with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Riots and Love

RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS is a magnificent document of its time.” –COLOGNE CINEMA NIGHTSCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: His Kind of Woman
screenings.description: While gambling houses have existed as long as societies have, the nefarious business model of the modern casino has infiltrated every facet of the American economy. No current sporting event can be broadcast without some adjacent ads for the ever-growing list of online sportsbooks; celebrities shill browser-based casinos like Stake, and while the Big Apple hasn’t succumbed its real estate to Big Gambling (yet), we here at Spectacle are encouraging irresponsible financial behavior with three noir stories focused on one of humanity’s oldest vices.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
