screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Sans Soleil
screenings.description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: zi
screenings.description: “Poetic, political, and above all incontrovertibly material” [The New Yorker], Kogonada’s fourth feature, the experimental drama zi, follows the title character, played by Michelle Mao, a concert violinist whose aimless peregrinations through the streets of Hong Kong are interrupted by visions of what may be either her past or future, a condition she attempts to explain to a new American acquaintance (Haley Lu Richardson, Columbus) while a stranger (Jin Ha) observes the pair from a distance. A valentine to the textures and colors of the Fragrant Harbor as seen by night, featuring music by the late Ryuichi Sakamoto, the formally audacious, shot-on-the-fly zi is a film of unusual delicacy and reserve, one whose air of mystery abides long after the credits have rolled.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: Paper Tiger in 35mm
screenings.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Sneak Preview: Paper Tiger with James Gray in person
screenings.description: Dir. James Gray. 2026, 115 mins. U.S. DCP. With Adam Driver, Scarlett Johnansson, Miles Teller, Gavin Goudey, Roman Engel. Recreating a finely rendered—and personally remembered—New York of the mid 1980s, James Gray has constructed a classical moral drama of tragic proportions that is among his greatest achievements. Equal parts tender and sinister, the film stars Adam Driver as Gary Pearl, a former NYC police officer who tries to help his middle-class Queens family man brother Irving (a tremendous Miles Teller) make some extra money for wife and teenage boys by looping him in on a “sure thing” deal with some local Russians working the Gowanus Canal in Brooklyn. Of course, all doesn’t go as planned, and the film charts the mounting, fearful consequences of this get-rich-quick scheme. A deeply felt tale of loyalty and sacrifice, Paper Tiger features expressive widescreen photography and sensationally moving performances from Driver, Teller, and Johansson, who’s mesmerizing as Irving’s wife Hester, clinging to terrible secrets of her own. This is a free preview screening, courtesy of NEON. Reservations will open soon with priority given to MoMI members.

screenings.title: Postcolonial Motion: Taxis and Travelogues
screenings.description: While not as long-standing as the romance with trains, cinema has a love affair with taxis. A cab ride is often more than just a means of getting from one place to another. The taxi is a cinematic apparatus in motion, a confessional, an urban microcosm, a transition, a temporary intimacy, an archive of daily life, a nightmare of forced conversation, an eavesdropper’s dream. Yet beneath such metaphors are material threats: the gig economy, prior and enduring precarities and exploitation of labor, movements of migration conditioned by colonization.POSTCOLONIAL MOTION: TAXIS AND TRAVELOGUES draws together three films combining oral testimonies and the kinetics of transport. Frank Sweeney, Karimah Ashadu, and Timoteus Anggawan Kusno each consider the movements of people, goods and images, tracing how workers warp the barriers of historical categories and economic constraints as they cross borders.Guest-programmed by Yasmina Price, who wrote the introduction and individual film descriptions.Frank SweeneyGO YE AFAR2026, 24 min, DCPIrish research-based artist Frank Sweeney’s latest work, GO YE AFAR (2026), stages a historical examination of economy, religion, national identity, and state power through the nocturnal taxi journey of a Nigerian driver in Dublin and Calabar. Making a link between the IMF’s role in imposing a debt structure on Ireland in the 2010s and the economic dependency still inflicted on the African continent, Sweeney makes a taxi journey an illuminating lens onto the dubious legacies of Catholic missionaries and European philanthropy, global privatization and the erosion of the commons.Karimah AshaduBROWN GOODS2020, 12 min, DCPBROWN GOODS (2020), by British-born Nigerian artist and director Karimah Ashadu, both shares and reconfigures a similar terrain. The film scans the intermingled economies and geographies of Africa and Europe, conjuring Nigeria from its viewpoint in Germany. The setting is specifically Hamburg, a hub of international trade and multinational corporations. Ashadu’s agile camerawork delves through docks, weaving amongst ship containers and stacks of tires as Emeka – the self-sufficient central figure, excluded from formal work due to his humanitarian status – voices a sharp analysis of manufacturing and industrial monopolies, the politics of resources and global capital.Timoteus Anggawan KusnoOBSCURA2026, 14 min, DCPIndonesian filmmaker and visual artist Timoteus Anggawan Kusno’s OBSCURA (2026) echoes the unsettling, spectral dreaminess and mediatized archival memory of GO YE AFAR. Operating between Indonesia and the Netherlands, the film critically reworks the form of the ethnographic travelogue and colonial imagery through a story of theft (another kind of informal job). Gallery workers liberate a painting and carry it out in a truck, performing how images physically travel, are taken apart, literally unframed and reframed.Total running time: ca. 55 min.The screening will be followed by a conversation with filmmaker and artist Frank Sweeney!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Narrow Rooms: Drunken Noodles
screenings.description: Lucio CastroDRUNKEN NOODLES2025, 83 min, DCP. In English and Spanish with English subtitles.When Adnan (Laith Khalifeh) arrives in New York to work at a Lower East Side gallery for the summer, he’s newly single and ready to mingle. He cruises strangers in the park at night and begins a flirtation with a delivery driver. At work, he’s helping to exhibit the recently discovered work of Sal Salandra, a real-world gay artist and elder who crafts tableaus of gay orgies and sex club scenes in vibrant needlepoint. These artworks – and Sal himself, played by Ezriel Kornel – become the connective thread for a time-jumping narrative that unfolds in four parts. Made for little money, with a small crew and total creative control, the latest by Lucio Castro (END OF THE CENTURY) is a delightful, sexually-charged short-story collection with whimsical elements of dreamy magical realism. Released during the full flower of NYC PRIDE season, DRUNKEN NOODLES is well worth watching – or rewatching – before making your Best-of-2026 lists.We’ll be joined by director Lucio Castro and cast members for a Q&A following the screening!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: If fans of previous Spectacle classic Payday are looking for another downbeat 1973 road movie by a Canadian director about a deeply toxic country singer, they should look no further than The Hard Part Begins. Donnelly Rhodes inhabits King with a mixture of charm and bitterness that befits the character’s big-fish small-pond aspirations, while future Prom Night director Paul Lynch finds a ramshackle beauty in its world of van journeys and dive bars. The Hard Part Begins presages Inside Llewyn Davis in its balance of an unforgiving portrait of its protagonist with a sympathy for the also-rans following their artistic ambitions to the bitter end.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Mouse
screenings.description: It’s 2002, and best friends Minnie and Callie are heading into their senior year of high school, with Minnie long living in the protective shadow of the charismatic and admired Callie. When their friendship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer, Minnie struggles to define her own identity and forms a complicated relationship with Callie’s poised, attentive mother, pulling her further from her own chaotic home.

The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.description: A garish amalgam of Westworld and The Mummy, Passeri’s 2000 masterpiece addresses the controversial practice of planting microchips in mummies in order to staff fantasy theme parks. Transcending its influences, the film boasts a uniquely queasy visual style crafted from greasy animatronics and a painfully saturated color palette. The plot concerns two dimwitted American journalists caught in the meltdown of the titular Mummy Theme Park – this, of course, is of secondary significance beside the exercise in discount worldmaking achieved through Passeri’s fabric-store scenography and a script rife with non-sequiturs.

screenings.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
screenings.description: The year before enjoying enormous popular success with The Favourite, Lanthimos rolled out perhaps his most difficult and disquieting film to date, a Greek tragedy transplanted to the American suburbs starring Colin Farrell as Steven Murphy, a cardiothoracic surgeon who opens his home in an unguarded moment to a fatherless 16-year-old (Barry Keoghan)… and, as it happens, to a terrible retribution that threatens Murphy’s wife (Nicole Kidman), teenaged daughter, and adolescent son. “A typically arch dramatic conundrum, laced with Lanthimos’s trademark off-kilter artifice and deadpan humour… An increasingly sickening hunger game driven by an inflexible moral imperative.” —The Observer

screenings.title: zi
screenings.description: “Poetic, political, and above all incontrovertibly material” [The New Yorker], Kogonada’s fourth feature, the experimental drama zi, follows the title character, played by Michelle Mao, a concert violinist whose aimless peregrinations through the streets of Hong Kong are interrupted by visions of what may be either her past or future, a condition she attempts to explain to a new American acquaintance (Haley Lu Richardson, Columbus) while a stranger (Jin Ha) observes the pair from a distance. A valentine to the textures and colors of the Fragrant Harbor as seen by night, featuring music by the late Ryuichi Sakamoto, the formally audacious, shot-on-the-fly zi is a film of unusual delicacy and reserve, one whose air of mystery abides long after the credits have rolled.

screenings.title: Je t'aime, je t'aime
screenings.description: A “quiet mixture of science fiction with a love story as subtle as anything in Rohmer or Rivette” [Raymond Durgnat], Resnais’s definition-defying film stars Claude Rich as an unsuccessful suicide who, on leaving hospital, agrees to participate in an experiment in time travel—one that will bring fragments of his past rushing back is disordered shards.

screenings.title: Barbara
screenings.description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin.Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Playback
screenings.description: On the edge of his 40th birthday Haji (Jun Murakami), an actor haunted by dreams of his own death, accepts an invitation from an old friend to revisit his hometown for a wedding—only to doze off en route and wake to find himself in the school uniform of his youth, seemingly catapulted back into the past. A remarkably mature, circumspect depiction of middle-age morass and melancholia from a director who was only in his mid-twenties when he made it, Playback’s premiere at the 2012 Locarno Film Festival established Miyake as a filmmaker to watch. A work of bold experimentation and teasing ambiguity, described by his friend Ryusuke Hamaguchi as “like a modern-day reincarnation of [John Cassavetes’s] Opening Night.”

screenings.title: Harakiri, I Miss You + Q&A
screenings.description: Three young friends wander through Madrid over 24 hours, tangled in rivalry and fragile masculinity. Obsessed with an older woman who teases and rejects them, they face encounters that push them to the edge—a raw portrait of youth lost between desire and emotional violence.

screenings.title: Cabaret
screenings.description: Dir. Bob Fosse. 1972, 124 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Liza Minnelli, Michael York, Helmut Griem, Joel Grey, Maria Berenson. Fosse rightly won the Best Director Oscar for his shattering musical set in Berlin on the eve of Hitler’s rise to power. Liza Minnelli and Joel Grey also scored Oscars for their unforgettable performances as, respectively, Sally Bowles, a vivacious but damaged American singer selling her soul in a seedy nightclub, and the devilish emcee who presides over it. A devastating, delirious movie experience, featuring John Kander and Fred Ebb’s rousing show tunes and Geoffrey Unsworth’s gloriously ragged photography, Cabaret reinvented the movie musical for 1970s American cinema and all but wrote a new cinematic grammar for how to shoot and edit song and dance. screenings.title: In Bed with Victoria
screenings.description: High-powered lawyer Victoria (Efira) is an unstoppable force in the courtroom, but off the clock she struggles to raise her two daughters on her own, respond to the latest online defamation from her vindictive ex-husband, and feign more than passing interest in her latest app-arranged fuck-and-run. While wrapped up in a singularly unusual case brought to her by an old pal (Melvil Poupaud), Victoria reconnects with a onetime client (Vincent Lacoste) who seems to offer the prospect of something more than a desultory fling… that is, if she’s ready or able to accept what’s on offer. A frisky, funny showcase for Efira, unforgettable as the pouty, rumpled, restless, reckless Victoria, smart and savvy in its upending of rom-com cliché.

screenings.title: Crystal Voyager
screenings.description: Directed by Elfick, co-founder of the Australian surf magazine Tracks, “the Citizen Kane of surfing pictures” [The Guardian] follows photographer, filmmaker, and avid surfer George Greenough, as well as fellow wave-chasers Nat Young and Richie West, on a quest for secluded surf spots that goes from coastal California to Lennox Head, New South Wales, to points even further afield. A heady paean to the elements, to sun and water, whose fisheye tube-riding POV shots were received as nothing short of revolutionary when it premiered, and whose psychedelic soundtrack by The Crystal Voyager Band won it an ardent following in counterculture hot spots the world over.

screenings.title: The Landlord | The Ravishing Cinema of Bill Gunn
screenings.description: Written by visionary black filmmaker Bill Gunn and the first film of Oscar-winning director Hal Ashby, The Landlord is both a coming-of-age tale and a social satire. When wealthy, white Elger Winthrop Enders buys a tenement brownstone in pre-gentrified Park Slope Brooklyn, he plans to evict its predominantly Black residents. Instead, he becomes entangled in the lives of his tenants.

Argento uses the occasion to scale new, dizzying heights of his own, employing bravura crane shots, brazenly baroque lighting, and the iconic moment of a razor slashing through white cotton.

screenings.title: Drive
screenings.description: Drawing inspiration from Walter Hill’s The Driver, Refn’s high-style tour-de-force stars Ryan Gosling as a loner Los Angeles stunt driver who moonlights as a getaway wheelman on armed stickups, who’s put on a collision course with a nefarious criminal syndicate thanks to his protective affection for neighbor Carey Mulligan. A terse, tough, and morosely moody film propelled by a shimmering synth-pop score, with an extraordinary supporting cast that includes an against-type Albert Brooks as a sullen, profane gangster kingpin.

screenings.description: Whilst on a short weekend getaway, Louise shoots a man who had tried to rape Thelma. Due to the incriminating circumstances, they make a run for it and thus a cross country chase ensues for the two fugitives. Along the way, both women rediscover the strength of their friendship and surprising aspects of their personalities and self-strengths in the trying times.

screenings.title: Over the Hedge
screenings.description: When Verne (Garry Shandling) and fellow woodland friends awake from winter’s hibernation, they find they have some new neighbors: humans, and RJ (Bruce Willis), an opportunistic raccoon who shows the others how to exploit the suburban bounty laid out before them.

screenings.title: Les rendez-vous d'Anna
screenings.description: Akerman’s third feature was this transfixing—and, one suspects, quite personal—study of alienation and emotional withdrawal, in which a well-known Belgian director (Aurore Clément), traveling the increasingly homogenized cities of Western Europe to promote her latest movie, eavesdrops on conversations and passes through a series of brief encounters with acquaintances old and new, including a one-night stand with Helmut Griem, a reconnection with ex-lover Jean-Pierre Cassel, and a stiff reception from aloof mother Lea Massari.

screenings.title: The Souvenir
screenings.description: Hogg, who has quietly established herself as one of the finest UK filmmakers working, offers a keenly observed, sometimes bruising portrayal of toxic romance set in ’80s Britain, starring Honor Swinton Byrne (daughter of Tilda, who plays the character’s patrician mother) as Julie, an aspiring filmmaker who begins a relationship with Anthony (Tom Burke), a slightly older man in the employ of the Foreign Office whose attractive intelligence and worldliness can’t compensate for the fact that he is an addict and a natural manipulator. Hogg’s usual compositional rigor works in service of enormously empathic semi-autobiographical storytelling, using flashback inserts in order to plumb the psychology of a hopelessly dysfunctional relationship.

screenings.title: Some Came Running
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1958, 137 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Frank Sinatra, Shirley MacLaine, Dean Martin, Martha Hyer, Arthur Kennedy. Minnelli’s phenomenally directed and acted tale of rootlessness in post–World War II America stars Frank Sinatra as a war veteran and former writer who has fallen into alcoholism, and who returns to his Indiana hometown to find nothing is quite as he remembered it. Dean Martin is the unrepentant gambler whom he befriends, and Shirley MacLaine is heartbreaking in a signature early role as a wayward woman who limps after him, hoping he will love her. One of the great American melodramas of the 1950s, this CinemaScope adaptation of James Jones’s novel builds to a frenetic carnival climax that is among Minnelli’s finest achievements. screenings.description: Back in the ‘pre-code’ era of the 1920s and early 1930s, animated cartoons were made to entertain the adults in the audience. The results were often sexually suggestive, if not borderline explicit. Much later, with the long overdue relaxation of old censorship codes, independent and experimental animators of the 1960s and beyond became free to openly explore the raunchy and risqué once more. Salacious sexiness, lustful adultery, queerness, Peeping Toms, and other questionable—or perfectly human—adult behaviors were only some of the wonderfully ‘vulgar’ themes present in animated shorts made in both eras.

screenings.title: Shutter Island
screenings.description: An infamous triple filicide has escaped from Ashecliffe Hospital, located on a rugged islet in Boston Harbor that bears a striking resemblance to Arnold Böcklin’s Island of the Dead, and US Marshal Chuck Aule and his new partner (Leonardo DiCaprio and Mark Ruffalo) are on the scene to investigate. Set in the postwar period that gave birth to some of the most anguished of all film noir, Scorsese’s feverish thriller is awash in the psychic trauma of the mid-century, its soundtrack a catalog of jarring modernist classical compiled by collaborator Robbie Robertson and including work by Krzysztof Penderecki, John Cage, and Max Richter, among others, with Robert Richardson’s cinematography suggesting a particularly jaundiced, blighted version of the Technicolor process.

screenings.title: And Your Bird Can Sing preceded by August 8th
screenings.description: “Among Sho Miyake's most quietly luminous works, And Your Bird Can Sing is a tender and deeply felt portrait of youth poised between freedom and uncertainty. Adapted from Yasushi Sato's novel and set in the port city of Hakodate, the film follows three young adults drifting through work, friendship, and desire as summer gives way to an uncertain future. With its naturalistic performances, loose rhythms, and extraordinary sensitivity to time, place, and everyday gestures, Miyake finds profound emotional resonance in the ordinary, affirming his distinctive voice in contemporary Japanese cinema.” —Shun Inoue, Japan Foundation

screenings.title: Leave Her to Heaven
screenings.description: A chilling film noir like no other, Gene Tierney stars as Ellen Berent, a beautiful and possessive woman whose overly dependent love for her husband turns increasingly sinister. Shot in gorgeous technicolor by director John M. Stahl and DP Leon Shamroy (winner of the Academy Award for Best Color Cinematography), Leave Her to Heaven became 20th Century Fox’s highest-grossing film of the 1940’s. At the rotten center is an Oscar-nominated performance from Tierney, playing the rare femme fatale who isn’t motivated by all-American greed and ambition, but instead is consumed by obsession, jealousy, and deadly devotion.

screenings.title: Music Is Music + Before It’s Too Late
The French Connection
screenings.description: Dir. William Friedkin. 1971, 104 mins. DCP. With Gene Hackman, Roy Scheider, Fernando Rey, Tony Lo Bianco. “I felt this was a kind of crude poem to the city,” said director William Friedkin about this emotionally complex action masterpiece about an ethically dubious New York City cop, “Popeye” Doyle, who will do anything to take down a ring of foreign heroin smugglers. The justly celebrated car and elevated subway chase through Bensonhurst required an actual Transit Authority motorman on set and five weeks to complete. Friedkin’s breakthrough won Best Picture and four other Oscars, including Gene Hackman for Best Actor. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. screenings.description: American Baby follows Oli as she navigates the repercussions of being very young and very pregnant in small-town Texas. As she seeks out the suddenly absent teenage father-to-be of her child, Oli confronts the growing isolation from her community.

screenings.title: Ec: Intolerance
screenings.description: Griffith’s immensely influential silent epic intercuts four parallel tales from history (spanning Babylon, Christ’s Judea, Reformation Europe, and turn-of-the-century America) to embroider a moral tapestry on personal, social, and political repression through the ages. The visual poetry is overwhelming, especially in the massed crowd scenes, and the unbridled eroticism of the Babylon harem scenes demonstrates just what Hollywood lost when it later bowed to the Hays Code. While the (partly self-financed) production ruined Griffith financially and baffled audiences with its multiple plots and labyrinthine structure, it has been enormously influential on generations of filmmakers, including Eisenstein, who studied the film closely.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: All the Long Nights
screenings.description: Based on the novel of the same name by Maiko Seo, Miyake’s tender, understated drama stars Hokuto Matsumura and Mone Kamishiraishi as two co-workers who, after discovering they both suffer from invisibly debilitating conditions little understood by the wider world—he from blindsiding panic attacks, she from wild PMS-related mood swings—form a tentative bond based on mutual respect and care. Often affecting but never given to unearned sentiment, abhorrent of cliché, caricature, and easy scapegoating, All The Long Nights is a deeply humane film about the everyday hurdles faced in muddling through life, buoyed by the considerable chemistry of its irresistible leads.

screenings.title: Slither
screenings.description: “The first time I saw Slither was on VHS on a small television, in a friend’s East Village apartment, probably in 2005. It was raining outside and we got takeout from B&H Dairy, a perfect way to see this weird and funny movie. I’ve not found out much about it since, partly because there doesn’t seem to be that much to dig up, but also because I’ve never wanted to disrupt its strange magic.” —Nathan Gelgud

screenings.title: Dr. Strangelove Or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1964. 95 mins. 35mm. With Peter Sellers, George C. Scott, Sterling Hayden, Slim Pickens, Keenan Wynn. Stanley Kubrick reinvents the nuclear suspense thriller, then in vogue, as an absurdist black comedy in this brilliant evocation of cold war paranoia. Dr. Strangelove, co-written by Kubrick and Terry Southern, strikes just the right manic, irreverent, sexually charged tone, creating a satirical masterpiece that is one of the seminal counterculture works of the 1960s. Towering over the cast—which also includes George C. Scott as the blustering General Buck Turgidson and Sterling Hayden as “precious bodily fluids”–obsessed General Jack D. Ripper—is Sellers, a triple threat as meek RAF Captain Mandrake, bungling U.S. President Merkin Muffley, and, of course, the mad scientist title character—inventor of the doomsday machine that may wipe out humanity as we know it. screenings.description: Written by visionary black filmmaker Bill Gunn and the first film of Oscar-winning director Hal Ashby, The Landlord is both a coming-of-age tale and a social satire. When wealthy, white Elger Winthrop Enders buys a tenement brownstone in pre-gentrified Park Slope Brooklyn, he plans to evict its predominantly Black residents. Instead, he becomes entangled in the lives of his tenants.

screenings.title: The State of Things
screenings.description: German filmmaker Friedrich (Patrick Bauchau) is holed up at a hotel on the storm-lashed Portuguese coast, using American funding to shoot a shoestring budget post-apocalyptic thriller, though mostly he winds up playing a waiting game with cast and crew (including Warhol star Viva, Sam Fuller, Isabelle Weingarten, and co-writer Robert Kramer) after their producer disappears without a trace. An intermediate production made during the difficult shoot of Wenders’s 1982 Hammett for Francis Ford Coppola’s Zoetrope Studios in the US, sumptuously shot in black and white by legendary DP Henri Alekan, The State of Things is Wenders’s meditation on the complicated co-dependence of the European and American film industries.

screenings.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
screenings.description: The year before enjoying enormous popular success with The Favourite, Lanthimos rolled out perhaps his most difficult and disquieting film to date, a Greek tragedy transplanted to the American suburbs starring Colin Farrell as Steven Murphy, a cardiothoracic surgeon who opens his home in an unguarded moment to a fatherless 16-year-old (Barry Keoghan)… and, as it happens, to a terrible retribution that threatens Murphy’s wife (Nicole Kidman), teenaged daughter, and adolescent son. “A typically arch dramatic conundrum, laced with Lanthimos’s trademark off-kilter artifice and deadpan humour… An increasingly sickening hunger game driven by an inflexible moral imperative.” —The Observer

screenings.title: Ec: Eggeling / Grant / Jacobs & Fleischner
screenings.description: Viking EggelingSYMPHONIE DIAGONALE (1924, 8 min, 35mm, silent)“This early experimental short is one of only two films completed by Swedish-born artist Viking Eggeling, who worked in Paris, Milan, and ultimately Germany. It utilizes paper cutouts, tin foil, and frame-by-frame photography to create a playful show in which cubist, even art deco, circles and lines dance – diagonally – across the black screen.” –FACETSDwinell GrantCOMPOSITION #2 CONTRATHEMIS (1941, 5 min, 16mm, silent)“An attempt to develop visual abstract themes and to counterpoint them in a planned, formal composition.” –Dwinell GrantSTOP MOTION TESTS (1942, 3 min, 16mm, silent)A pixillated self-portrait of the filmmaker in his studio.COLOR SEQUENCE (1943, 3 min, 16mm, silent)“Pure solid-color frames which fade, mutate and flicker. A research into color rhythms and perceptual phenomena.” –William MoritzKen Jacobs & Bob FleischnerBLONDE COBRA1959-63, 35 min, 16mm-to-35mm blow-up. With Jack Smith. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from The Film Foundation.“BLONDE COBRA is an erratic narrative – no, not really a narrative, it’s only stretched out in time for convenience of delivery. It’s a look in on an exploding life, on a man of imagination suffering pre-fashionable Lower East Side deprivation and consumed with American 1950s, 40s, 30s disgust. Silly, self-pitying, guilt-strictured and yet triumphing – on one level – over the situation with style… enticing us into an absurd moral posture the better to dismiss us with a regal ‘screw off.’” –Ken JacobsTotal running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: Three young friends wander through Madrid over 24 hours, tangled in rivalry and fragile masculinity. Obsessed with an older woman who teases and rejects them, they face encounters that push them to the edge—a raw portrait of youth lost between desire and emotional violence.

screenings.title: Lost Highway
screenings.description: Few filmmakers have shown themselves so adept at plumbing the depths of the subconscious without coming up for air as Lynch, whose Lost Highway—inspired loosely by still-fresh coverage of the O. J. Simpson trial—begins as a dark domestic drama concerning a sexually incompetent saxophonist (Bill Pullman) and his wife (Patricia Arquette), morphs into a movie about a cocksman mechanic (Balthazar Getty) who gets involved with a gangster’s girl (Arquette, again), and ends with an unleashing of apocalyptic, purgative flame… Whether you take it as a cinematic depiction of a psychogenic fugue state or a free-associative disgorging of images from Hollywood’s id, Lynch’s film has the pull of a whirlpool and the terrible logic of a nightmare.

screenings.title: The Brood
screenings.description: In The Brood, the bitter divorce between the mentally disturbed Nola (Samantha Eggar) and her ex-husband Frank (Art Hindle) was pretty messy, so it should be a good sign that she’s finally getting professional help from the renowned Dr. Hal Raglan (Oliver Reed)—but Frank can’t help but notice that people on Nola’s long list of enemies keep dying at the hands of asexual, dwarfish assassins, and so he starts to wonder what exactly the experimental therapy practiced at Dr. Raglan’s Somafree Institute consists of… Written while Cronenberg was in the midst of his own divorce and custody battle, The Brood is a brutal, bracing airing of anxieties gussied up in grindhouse trappings.

screenings.title: zi
screenings.description: “Poetic, political, and above all incontrovertibly material” [The New Yorker], Kogonada’s fourth feature, the experimental drama zi, follows the title character, played by Michelle Mao, a concert violinist whose aimless peregrinations through the streets of Hong Kong are interrupted by visions of what may be either her past or future, a condition she attempts to explain to a new American acquaintance (Haley Lu Richardson, Columbus) while a stranger (Jin Ha) observes the pair from a distance. A valentine to the textures and colors of the Fragrant Harbor as seen by night, featuring music by the late Ryuichi Sakamoto, the formally audacious, shot-on-the-fly zi is a film of unusual delicacy and reserve, one whose air of mystery abides long after the credits have rolled.

screenings.title: Thelma & Louise
screenings.description: Whilst on a short weekend getaway, Louise shoots a man who had tried to rape Thelma. Due to the incriminating circumstances, they make a run for it and thus a cross country chase ensues for the two fugitives. Along the way, both women rediscover the strength of their friendship and surprising aspects of their personalities and self-strengths in the trying times.

screenings.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Classic Shorts
screenings.description: Along with the Academy Award–winning success of Aardman Animations’ 1990 Creature Comforts, it was this trio of inspired shorts featuring cheese-loving, jug-eared, Wigan-based crackpot inventor Wallace and his erudite pet dog/straight man/frequent savior Gromit that established the company as a stop-motion dynasty to delight all ages. Featuring A Grand Day Out, in which Wallace whips up a homemade spaceship in order to sample lunar cheddar; The Wrong Trousers, in which nefarious penguin Feathers McGraw employs a new Wallace patent in a daring heist; and A Close Shave, in which our heroes must step away from their window washing concern to foil a sheep rustling operation.

screenings.title: Over the Hedge
screenings.description: When Verne (Garry Shandling) and fellow woodland friends awake from winter’s hibernation, they find they have some new neighbors: humans, and RJ (Bruce Willis), an opportunistic raccoon who shows the others how to exploit the suburban bounty laid out before them.

screenings.title: The Long, Long Trailer
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1953, 96 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Lucille Ball, Desi Arnaz, Marjorie Main, Keenan Wynn. Lucy and Desi and Minnelli? Talk about a dream team. In this hilarious mix of romantic comedy, slapstick, and suspense, Ball and Arnaz—at the time the two most popular performers in the nation—play Tacy and Nicky (of course), an engaged couple who purchase a trailer so they can journey the country and play at domesticity before tying the knot. Aside from getting to see America’s favorite redhead in Technicolor, The Long, Long Trailer, the only major big-screen outing for the TV icons, offers up the perfect premise for a 1950s comedy, commenting on the comforts of postwar material culture with escalating madcap brilliance. screenings.title: Benedetta
screenings.description: Inspired by the life of Benedetta Carlini, a nun of 17th-century Tuscany whose claims of mystic visions drew the attention of church higher-ups, their investigations eventually revealing a verboten sexual relationship between Carlini and one of her fellow nuns and leading to her imprisonment, Verhoeven’s earthy, irreverent film immerses one in the squelchy squalor and earthly delights of Counter-Reformation era Europe, with Virginie Efira a revelation in the title role and Charlotte Rampling, as the abbess of the convent, conveying roiling inner turmoil beneath a cooly composed exterior. An examination of the difficult relationship between religious submission and sexual liberation, featuring some of the most memorable foley sounds in recent cinema.

screenings.title: The Souvenir
screenings.description: Hogg, who has quietly established herself as one of the finest UK filmmakers working, offers a keenly observed, sometimes bruising portrayal of toxic romance set in ’80s Britain, starring Honor Swinton Byrne (daughter of Tilda, who plays the character’s patrician mother) as Julie, an aspiring filmmaker who begins a relationship with Anthony (Tom Burke), a slightly older man in the employ of the Foreign Office whose attractive intelligence and worldliness can’t compensate for the fact that he is an addict and a natural manipulator. Hogg’s usual compositional rigor works in service of enormously empathic semi-autobiographical storytelling, using flashback inserts in order to plumb the psychology of a hopelessly dysfunctional relationship.

screenings.title: Losing Ground | The Ravishing Cinema of Bill Gunn
screenings.description: The inimitable Kathleen Collins’s second film tells the story of two remarkable people, married and hurtling toward a crossroads in their lives: Sara Rogers, a Black professor of philosophy, is embarking on an intellectual quest just as her painter husband, Victor, sets off on an exploration of joy. Victor decides to rent a country house away from the city, but the couple’s summer idyll becomes complicated by his involvement with a younger model. One of the very first fictional features by an African-American woman, Losing Ground remains a stunning and powerful work of art for being a funny, brilliant, and personal member of indie cinema canon.

screenings.title: Maîtres Anciens – Comédie
screenings.description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseillePreceded by:Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. With Barbara Hannigan.)“In C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE, I explore a mystery that fascinates me: where do these inhuman voices come from? screenings.title: Hold Onto Me
screenings.description: Dir. Myrsini Aristidou. 2026, 102 mins. Greece. DCP. In Greek with English subtitles. With Maria Petrova, Christos Passalis, Jenny Sallo. It’s summer, and plucky 11-year-old Iris is running wild through the streets with her friend Danae when she discovers that her estranged father, Aris, is back in town for his father’s funeral. Determined to know him, Iris tracks him down to a dilapidated shipyard, where he’s been keeping to himself. What begins as a stubborn attempt to reconnect slowly unfolds into a fragile, imperfect, yet poignant bond. Hold Onto Me won the Sundance 2026 Audience Award in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition and is the first-ever Cyprus submission for the Best International Feature Oscar. Christos Passalis won the 2026 New York Greek Film Expo Award for Best Performance by an Actor. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. screenings.title: Somewhere in the Night
screenings.description: Mankiewicz’s sophomore effort as director was this sinisterly atmospheric, baroquely plotted, deliriously disorienting “nervous nightmare” [The Village Voice] starring John Hodiak as an amnesiac ex-Marine who returns to his native Los Angeles to trawl its nightclubs, sanitariums, and docks in search of clues to his identity and traces of a mysterious stranger by the name of “Larry Cravat.” It’s a mission that puts him in close contact with the criminal underworld and a rogue’s gallery of unusual characters (Richard Conte, Josephine Hutchinson, and Fritz Kortner are on-hand in piquant supporting parts) while tying him up in a hunt for Nazi-plundered treasure.

screenings.title: Lorraine O'Grady: Rivers, First Draft Performance
The Cobweb
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1955, 134 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Lauren Bacall, Richard Widmark, Gloria Grahame, Lillian Gish, Charles Boyer, John Kerr, Susan Strasberg, Oscar Levant. An essential Minnelli, featuring maybe his most wildly stacked cast, The Cobweb confidently offers up a nearly undefinable mix of the restrained and the truly eccentric. Set in a psychiatric hospital, where the staff is likely more unsettled than the patients, this Cinemascope, Eastmancolor contraption details the fallout after the head doctor’s wife does the unthinkable: she changes the color of the library’s drapes! Long read as a perfect auteur text for Minnelli (who got his start as a window dresser), The Cobweb is a gorgeously shot, low-boil soap opera that’s a must for any 1950s melodrama completist. UNE SIMPLE HISTOIRE is, more than a narrative, a formal stylistic exercise so rigorously disciplined and understated that it makes the visual asceticism of Robert Bresson seem almost Fellini-esque by comparison.” –TIMECLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Cockpit
screenings.description: The “cockpit” of the title is a cramped apartment in the suburbs of Tokyo, unprepossessing in size but bursting with creative ferment, for this dinky flat is functioning as the recording studio where underground producer-rapper OMSB and cohort Bim are laying down a new track, to be titled “Curve Death Match.” Shot largely from a camera locked down to the workstation and facing the duo, The Cockpit follows the songwriting process from sampling to beat-making to writing to the final recording, in the process giving an intimate, pared-to-the-bone, nuts-and-bolts breakdown of the intricacies of hip-hop artistry without rival.

screenings.title: Ec: Jerome Hill
screenings.description: These 35mm prints are the result of a preservation project undertaken by the Museum of Modern Art.DEATH IN THE FORENOON (1934/66, 2 min, 35mm)CANARIES (1969, 4 min, 35mm)&FILM PORTRAIT(1971, 81 min, 35mm)“FILM PORTRAIT is an autobiography in the sense that it deals explicitly with Jerome’s most personal life’s relationship to film. It draws on film clips taken in his childhood and his whole childhood involvement in art and life. It comes closest to any kind of filmic answer to Proust. […] FILM PORTRAIT is, I believe, the only direct autobiography we have in film. There is Jonas Mekas’s WALDEN, which is diary but not autobiography in a strict sense. We have Cocteau’s BLOOD OF A POET, ORPHEUS, and TESTAMENT OF ORPHEUS. One could say that this last is autobiographical, but it is also allusive and poetic; whereas Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT is a very straight attempt to present autobiography on film. Of course, subsequently, James Broughton’s TESTAMENT and my own SINCERITY & DUPLICITY series of autobiographical films were very much inspired by Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT as well as by Jonas’s WALDEN. […] Jerome Hill’s films are great because they are poised on wit and achieve a balance – a gentle, intentional, particularly American balance.” –Stan Brakhage, FILM AT WIT’S ENDTotal running time: ca. 90 min.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: The opening salvo in Dogme 95’s all-out assault on cinematic artifice, revolutionary in its emancipated use of the Sony DCR-PC7 Handycam, Vinterberg’s scorched earth melodrama/farce takes place during a gathering of the extended Hansen clan at a family-run hotel to mark the 60th birthday of solid burgher patriarch Helge (Henning Moritzen)—an event that takes a turn for the chaotic when Helge’s eldest son, Christian (Ulrich Thomsen), accuses his father of molesting both himself and his recently deceased twin sister during a dinner table toast. screenings.title: Detour
screenings.description: Hearing a certain tune spin on the jukebox in an all-night diner in Reno sends down-on-his-luck pianist Al Roberts (Tom Neal) on a traumatic trip down memory lane, recalling his fateful roadside encounter with Ann Savage’s aptly named femme fatale Vera and his subsequent subjugation to her, in Ulmer’s made-for-peanuts classic of noir absurdism, one of the priceless treasures to emerge from Hollywood’s so-called “Poverty Row” studios. “Possibly the bleakest, most doom-laden film noir ever… Savage’s sensational performance, combined with the real-life trajectory of Neal, who ended up going to prison for murdering his wife, have made this a tormented film with the despairing logic of nightmare.” —The Los Angeles Times

screenings.title: Ec: Hugo / Jacobs / Levitt / Maas
screenings.description: Ian HugoBELLS OF ATLANTIS(1952, 10 min, 16mm. Preserved by the Library of Congress through the Avant-Garde Masters program funded by The Film Foundation and administered by the National Film Preservation Foundation.)A film poem, based on Anaïs Nin’s HOUSE OF INCEST, narrated by and featuring Nin.“[BELLS OF ATLANTIS was] inspired by the prologue to my HOUSE OF INCEST and the line: ‘I remember my first birth in water.’ The film evoked the watery depths of the lost continent of Atlantis. It is a lyrical journey into prenatal memories, the theme of birth and rebirth from the sea.” –Anaïs NinKen JacobsLITTLE STABS AT HAPPINESS (1959-63, 18 min, 16mm. With Jack Smith.)“Material was cut in as it came out of the camera, embarrassing moments intact. 100’ rolls timed well with music on old 78s. I was interested in immediacy, a sense of ease, and an art where suffering was acknowledged but not trivialized with dramatics. Whimsy was our achievement, as well as breaking out of step.” –Ken JacobsHelen Levitt, Janice Loeb, and James AgeeIN THE STREET (1952, 12 min, 16mm, silent. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.)“Informality is indeed the crucial and virtually definitive quality of IN THE STREET; it is even the guiding principle and vision. […] This is the extreme realization of a classic ‘naturalistic’ genre, the German ‘street film,’ where the street was imaged as the arena of the everyday and random, the channel in which the ‘stream of life’ conveniently became microcosmic.” –Ken Kelman, THE ESSENTIAL CINEMAWillard MaasGEOGRAPHY OF THE BODY (1943, 7 min, 16mm, b&w. Preserved by Anthology with support from The National Film Preservation Foundation.)“The terrors and splendors of the human body as the undiscovered, mysterious continent.” –Willard MaasTotal running time: ca. 55 min.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.title: Devo: Restorations and Revelations
screenings.description: COLLECTED FILM AND VIDEO WORKS 1976-84PRESENTED BY FILM RESTORATIONIST PETER CONHEIMFormed in the wreckage of the Kent State shootings in 1973, where co-founders Gerald V. Casale and Mark Mothersbaugh were students during the massacre, and still blowing the horn five decades later, Akron’s DEVO would take their subversive pop-art to staggering mainstream success. All the while, they considered themselves to be filmmakers as much as they were a “band.”From their first film onward (1976’s THE BEGINNING WAS THE END: THE TRUTH ABOUT DE-EVOLUTION), they fused their love of Dadaist image-making with their constantly shapeshifting music, confounding their record label by plowing their meager promo budgets into companion films for songs. This program unveils painstaking new restorations and reconstructions of much of this pivotal work (including SATISFACTION, FREEDOM OF CHOICE, WHIP IT, and much more) alongside a host of rarely (and never)-seen live footage, encounters with hapless interviewers, and other spud ephemera, curated specially for Anthology Film Archives by film archivist and musician Peter Conheim (Mono Pause, ex-Negativland, Wet Gate, et al).Total running time: ca. 80 min + discussion and Q&A.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Broadcast News
screenings.description: A high-strung news producer finds herself in a love triangle between a talented but self-doubting reporter and a charming new anchor, who embodies the growing trivialization of news that she is determined to fight against. Cast William Hurt Albert Brooks Holly Hunter Robert Prosky Lois Chiles Joan Cusack Peter Hackes Christian Clemenson Jack Nicholson Robert Katims

screenings.title: Club Kid in 35mm
screenings.description: A hard-partying New York City club promoter sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

screenings.title: Paper Tiger in 35mm
screenings.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: How to Marry a Millionaire
screenings.description: Schatze Page, Loco Dempsey and Pola Debevoise (Lauren Bacall, Betty Grable, Marilyn Monroe) are three women on a mission: They all want to marry a millionaire. To accomplish this task, they move into a fancy New York City apartment and begin courting the city's elite. They have no problem meeting rich men, but unfortunately most of them turn out to be creeps or cons. Eventually they must decide: Is a life of luxury more important to them than finding true love?

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.title: Tár + Live Performance | Instruments of Desire
screenings.description: From writer-producer-director Todd Field comes TÁR, starring Cate Blanchett as Lydia Tár, the celebrated chief conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic. We meet Tár at the height of her career, as she’s preparing both a book launch and a much-anticipated live recording of Mahler’s Fifth Symphony. Over the ensuing weeks, her life and career unravel as allegations of misconduct erode her carefully cultivated public image. The result is a searing examination of artistic authority, institutional politics, and the blurred boundary between mentorship and exploitation.

screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: Cyclops
screenings.description: A secret group of scientists believes grotesque human mutations may represent the next stage of evolution – and they are willing to use living women to prove it. When their latest experiment ends in disaster, the researchers hunt the streets for a new subject, accompanied by a mysterious one-eyed mutant hiding behind dark glasses. Their obsession soon erupts into a delirious showdown of rupturing flesh, mutant bodies and spectacular practical gore in director Jôji Iida’s (Night Head, Ring, Spiral) notorious Japanese body-horror nightmare.

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall in 35mm
screenings.description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. He reminds us about the painful past, explains the present, and warns about the future. His dramatic plea, "do not be indifferent!" remains more relevant now than ever. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.title: Galaxie
screenings.description: A pinnacle of the art of filmic portraiture, Gregory Markopoulos’s GALAXIE comprises thirty short portraits of men and women from across the spectrum of the mid-1960s cultural scene in New York City. Its subjects include many of Markopoulos’s fellow experimental filmmakers – Storm De Hirsch, George & Mike Kuchar, Jonas Mekas, Shirley Clarke, Amy Taubin, and Ed Emshwiller – as well as figures from the literary and art worlds, including Parker Tyler, Jasper Johns, W.H. Auden, Allen Ginsberg, Kenneth Kelman, Maurice Sendak, Susan Sontag, and others. In keeping with Markopoulos’s short-form masterpieces MING GREEN, BLISS, and SORROWS, each of the individual portraits in GALAXIE was edited entirely in-camera, a near-miraculous feat given the intricate use of multiple layers of superimposition, all of it achieved by rewinding and making additional passes through the single 100-foot (ca. 3-minute) roll of 16mm film during the shoot. Initially intending to produce only a handful of portraits, Markopoulos ended up filming 40 different chapters, and ultimately incorporated the first 30 into the completed work (presented in the order they were created). Each of the portraits represents an exquisite visual record of the encounter between subject and filmmaker, while the film as a whole provides an extraordinary opportunity to observe the gradual development of Markopoulos’s approach to portraiture and in-camera editing.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Lolita
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1962. 152 mins. 35mm. With James Mason, Shelley Winters, Peter Sellers, Sue Lyon. “How did they ever make a movie of Lolita?” the savvy, shocked poster tagline wondered. Only Stanley Kubrick would dare try. Outwitting the censors, Kubrick turned Vladimir Nabokov’s 1955 novel about a professor’s obsession with a young “nymphet” into a rich cinematic satire, emphasizing Nabokov’s dark social comedy. A monstrously proper James Mason is unforgettable as Humbert Humbert, whose twisted heart leads him to destroy his own life and soul for the love of the teenage daughter (Sue Lyon) of his crass and lovelorn landlady (Shelley Winters). As the mysterious oddball playwright Clare Quilty, Sellers lends Kubrick’s tragic satire a coherent sense of eccentricity and outlandish humor. screenings.description: German filmmaker Friedrich (Patrick Bauchau) is holed up at a hotel on the storm-lashed Portuguese coast, using American funding to shoot a shoestring budget post-apocalyptic thriller, though mostly he winds up playing a waiting game with cast and crew (including Warhol star Viva, Sam Fuller, Isabelle Weingarten, and co-writer Robert Kramer) after their producer disappears without a trace. An intermediate production made during the difficult shoot of Wenders’s 1982 Hammett for Francis Ford Coppola’s Zoetrope Studios in the US, sumptuously shot in black and white by legendary DP Henri Alekan, The State of Things is Wenders’s meditation on the complicated co-dependence of the European and American film industries.

Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Max Turnheim
screenings.description: Few contemporary filmmakers have demonstrated such a sustained commitment to the form of cinematic portraiture as Friedl vom Gröller, whose work is represented throughout this series. While most of her films are notably (and proudly) small in scale, MAX TURNHEIM is an exception, an ever-expanding collection of portraits of a subject she has returned to repeatedly throughout the years.“An allegorical reflection upon physiosocial existence in the world. This to-date 13-part, long-term portrait of Max Turnheim brings the abundance of Friedl vom Gröller’s gaze to complete fruition. The film conceives its portrait through the compression of an entire phase of life, including separation from the parental home, the finding of an individual path, and a renewed longing for middle class institutions. The point of departure for all this content is a face seen over the course of time.” –Alejandro BachmannCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: Dir. Frank Oz. U.S., 1984, 94 mins. U.S. DCP. With Jim Henson, Dave Goelz, Jerry Nelson, Richard Hunt, Steve Whitmire, Liza Minnelli. When the Muppets’ college revue is a big hit, they decide to take the show all the way to Broadway. Adjusting to the hustle and bustle of New York City, Kermit takes a job at a local restaurant while he searches for a producer. Filled with cameos by quintessential New Yorkers, such as Gregory Hines, Joan Rivers, James Coco, Brooke Shields, and Liza Minnelli, the movie ends with a fantastical and questionably genuine wedding between Kermit and Miss Piggy. Oz’s first solo-directed film is a dose of pure joy, a true gift to showtune lovers featuring some of the greatest songs in the Muppet canon and the beloved “Muppet Babies” sequence that spawned its own mini-franchise. Rated: G Preceded by: The Muppet Show Episode 414: Starring Liza Minnelli 1979, 23 mins. Liza Minnelli brought her many talents to The Muppet Show in its fourth season in 1979. In one of the handful of episodes that broke the show’s regular variety format, Liza headlines a Muppet murder mystery as an actress who hires private eye Kermit to solve a backstage crime—her show at the Roxy has been threatened by an anonymous culprit. In between the intrigue and dead bodies that keep turning up, Liza manages to deliver some top-notch musical numbers. Can Liza and Kermit solve the crime before the villain runs out of victims? screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.title: Sibyl
screenings.description: Four years before her Palme d’Or triumph with Anatomy of a Fall, Triet produced this comic thriller starring Virginie Efira in the title role as a psychotherapist who, fed up with her métier, decides to return to writing fiction—and, in the person of one of her patients, a young, tumultuous actress named Margot (Adèle Exarchopoulos), finds an absolutely irresistible source of literary inspiration. Impassioned performances by both leads make Sibyl a compelling study in obsession and self-delusion, with the added inducement of Anatomy star Sandra Hüller’s appearance in a side-splitting role as the director of a film-within-the-film.

screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 1
screenings.description: "“Gunvor Nelson launched her film career with a pair of raucous collage films made with her friend Dorothy Wiley. In Schmeerguntz, glamorized images of American womanhood clash with the reality of messy diapers and clogged kitchen sinks, revealing ‘a society which hides its animal functions beneath a shiny public surface’ (Film Quarterly). The surreal extravaganza Fog Pumas was a grand prize winner at the 1967 EXPRMTL festival in Knokke. My Name is Oona, perhaps Nelson’s best-known film, is an impressionistic portrait of her daughter with a memorably repetitive soundtrack partly created by Steve Reich. Kirsa Nicholina is at once a lyrical and boldly graphic birth film. Moons Pool, filmed entirely underwater with naked male and female bodies, is a dazzling example of Nelson’s visual and aural poetry. The serene Time Being is a loving, meditative film of Nelson’s mother, in bed, approaching death.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: Ec: Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son
In the Hand of Dante + Q&A
screenings.description: In the Hand of Dante follows the parallel lives of a New York author (Nick Tosches) in the 21st century who embarks on a violent journey after he is recruited by a mafia don to steal Italian poet Dante Alighieri’s The Divine Comedy written in the poet’s own hand, and Dante in the 14th century seeking inspiration to write his most important work – each man unknowingly connected through time and their obsessive quest for love, beauty, and the divine.

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.title: Paths of Glory
screenings.description: Preceded by Kubrick’s documentary short The Seafarers (1953, 30 mins) Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1957. 88 mins. 35mm. With Kirk Douglas, Ralph Meeker, Adolphe Menjou, George Macready, Wayne Morris, Richard Anderson. One of the bleakest anti-war films ever made, Stanley Kubrick’s brilliant World War I drama about the abuse of military hierarchy drives home its message in every aspect of its construction, from its mechanized tracking shots through trenches to its disturbingly protracted climax. Paths of Glory represents the first full expression of Kubrick’s style, but it also is the last of his films to center around a wholly virtuous hero (Douglas) and the last to view the human individual as a bulwark of decency in an inhuman world.
