screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: ACE Presents: Ghost World
screenings.description: The first film adaptation from the work of caustic cartoonist Daniel Clowes, Ghost World is a post-apocalyptic survival film set in the suburban AnyAmerica of 2001. Thora Birch and Scarlett Johansson co-star as two too-smart girls, freshly matriculated from high school and rudderless in early adulthood, who employ scalding irony as a ward to fend off the toxic effects of existence in a cultural wasteland, discovering an amiably creepy kindred spirit in the form of Steve Buscemi’s weedy record collector, Seymour. An anthem for opting out and modern-day classic, with editor Michael R. Miller displaying the gift for mordant, off-kilter comedy he’d honed working with the Coen Brothers.

screenings.title: Secrets & Lies
screenings.description: The winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1996 Cannes Film Festival, Leigh’s tender, funny, fearless film has Brenda Blethyn in a career-best performance as Cynthia, a white working-class woman who has a life-changing revelation when she meets Black middle-class optometrist Marianne Jean-Baptiste, who informs Cynthia she’s the little girl Cynthia had given up for adoption 27 years ago, all grown up. Developed, like all of Leigh’s films, through a process of collaborative improvisation, it’s a film of startling spontaneity and uncomfortable, unflinching emotional honesty.

screenings.title: Film No. 5 (smile)
screenings.description: “[S]hot with a high-speed camera…FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) reveals John Lennon’s face, recorded at 333 frames per second for an extended duration, outdoors, in color, and accompanied by a sound track of outdoor sounds recorded at the same time the imagery was recorded. FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) divides roughly into two halves, one continuous shot each. During the first half, the film is a meditation on Lennon’s face, which is so still that on first viewing I wasn’t entirely sure for a while that the film was live action and not an optically printed photograph of Lennon smiling slightly. Though almost nothing happens in any conventional sense, however, the intersection of the high speed filming and our extended gaze creates continuous, subtle transformations. […] While the second shot is more active than the first, the amount of activity remains minimal by conventional standards (and unusually so even for avant-garde film). It is as though those of us in the theater and Lennon are meditating on each other from opposite sides of the cinematic apparatus, joined together by Ono in a lovely, hypnotic stasis.” –Scott MacDonald, “Yoko Ono: Ideas on Film”Preceded by:Yoko OnoFLUXFILM NO. 16: aka NO. 4: BOTTOMS1966, 6 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent. Camera: Jeff Perkins, Anthony Cox. Starring: Susannah Campbell, Philip Corner, Anthony Cox, Bici Hendricks, Geoffrey Hendricks, Kyoko Ono, Yoko Ono, Ben Patterson, Jeff Perkins, Susan Poland, Jerry Sablo, Carolee Schneemann, James Tenney, Pieter Vanderbeck, Verne Williams.“The rebellious, erotic, liberatory nature of the film, which reflects the tenor of Fluxus, acts in direct opposition to the nineteenth-century scientific treatment of the body as a ‘dynamic field of action in need of regulation and control.’” –Chrissie Iles, “Erotic Conceptualism: The Films of Yoko Ono”Total running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Year of Living Dangerously
screenings.description: Dir. Peter Weir. 1983, 115 mins. Australia/U.S./Philippines. 35mm. With Mel Gibson, Sigourney Weaver, Linda Hunt. Bembol Rocco, Michael Murphy. Operating at the height of his storytelling powers, and following his international successes with Picnic at Hanging Rock and Gallipoli, Australian director Peter Weir took a big swing with this sweeping yet intimate historical drama. Set in Indonesia in the mid-sixties in the lead-up to the overthrow of President Sukarno’s government, Weir’s adaptation of Christopher Koch’s acclaimed novel centers around an Australian journalist (Gibson) and his romantic relationship with a British embassy officer (Weaver) and his professional one with a Chinese Australian photojournalist (Hunt, in an Oscar-winning performance). Suspenseful, romantic, and intelligent, the film predicted Weir’s remarkable run in Hollywood, yet stands on its own as a singular 1980s entertainment that traffics in politically complex themes with nuance and depth. screenings.title: Demons
screenings.description: Dir. Lamberto Bava. 1985, 88 min. DCP. With Natasha Hovey, Michele Soavi, Paolo Cazzo, Urbano Barberini, Karl Zinny. While attending the premiere of a horror movie, friends Cheryl (Hovey) and Kathy (Cazzo) find themselves trapped in the cinema from hell. Reality begins to imitate the film on the screen as members of the audience transform into ravenous demons and go on the rampage. A collaboration by producer Dario Argento and director Lamberto Bava, Demons is a marvel of bloody special effects by two Italian horror maestros that satirizes the idea that the Devil is lurking in every corner of the pop culture young people consume, waiting to corrupt and possess them. screenings.title: Barbara
screenings.description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin.Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
screenings.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: The Ascent
screenings.description: The bloodthirsty and seemingly unstoppable Nazi war machine is on the march towards Moscow in Shepitko’s wrenching, snow-swept World War II drama, which begins with two Soviet peasant soldiers foraging for food in a Belarusian village and proceeds to tell an emotional, lyrical tale of loyalty and betrayal, partisanship and collaboration, and, ultimately, the possibility of transcendent redemption. Shepitko’s final feature, frequently cited as among the greatest of Soviet films, won the Golden Bear at the 1977 Berlin Film Festival, just two years before its director’s tragic death in a car accident at age 41.

screenings.title: Benedetta
screenings.description: Inspired by the life of Benedetta Carlini, a nun of 17th-century Tuscany whose claims of mystic visions drew the attention of church higher-ups, their investigations eventually revealing a verboten sexual relationship between Carlini and one of her fellow nuns and leading to her imprisonment, Verhoeven’s earthy, irreverent film immerses one in the squelchy squalor and earthly delights of Counter-Reformation era Europe, with Virginie Efira a revelation in the title role and Charlotte Rampling, as the abbess of the convent, conveying roiling inner turmoil beneath a cooly composed exterior. An examination of the difficult relationship between religious submission and sexual liberation, featuring some of the most memorable foley sounds in recent cinema.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: Wendy Carlos’s score of switched-on Moog synthesizer classical, Kubrick’s punchy framings, and Malcolm McDowell’s cruelly charismatic, Nadsat slang-spouting performance as teen reprobate Alex combine to make for cracking cinema, and a hallucinatory imagination of a future broken Britain. Based on the stinging satire by Anthony Burgess, a work by turns exhilarating and nauseating, the film of A Clockwork Orange would be withdrawn from British cinemas at Kubrick’s behest, citing concern over reports that it had inspired copycat crimes in the UK.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. He reminds us about the painful past, explains the present, and warns about the future. His dramatic plea, "do not be indifferent!" remains more relevant now than ever. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Classic Shorts
screenings.description: Along with the Academy Award–winning success of Aardman Animations’ 1990 Creature Comforts, it was this trio of inspired shorts featuring cheese-loving, jug-eared, Wigan-based crackpot inventor Wallace and his erudite pet dog/straight man/frequent savior Gromit that established the company as a stop-motion dynasty to delight all ages. Featuring A Grand Day Out, in which Wallace whips up a homemade spaceship in order to sample lunar cheddar; The Wrong Trousers, in which nefarious penguin Feathers McGraw employs a new Wallace patent in a daring heist; and A Close Shave, in which our heroes must step away from their window washing concern to foil a sheep rustling operation.

screenings.title: The Rescuers
screenings.description: Geraldine Page, Bob Newhart, and Eva Gabor are among the vocal talent assembled for Disney’s vivacious adaptation of Margery Sharp’s beloved book series about the Rescue Aid Society, a group of dauntless mice who travel the world to lend aid to kidnapping victims. Here R.A.S. representatives Miss Bianca (Gabor) and Bernard (Newhart) rush to Devil’s Bayou, Louisiana, where they liberate a little girl named Penny from the clutches of the nefarious Madame Medusa (Page) and her trained crocodiles, Brutus and Nero, while at the same time tasked with keeping a precious gemstone safe from the villainess. A spirited, swashbuckling adventure, made with brio by Disney’s crack animation team led by rising star Don Bluth.

screenings.title: The Muppets Take Manhattan + The Muppet Show with Liza Minnelli
screenings.description: Dir. Frank Oz. U.S., 1984, 94 mins. U.S. DCP. With Jim Henson, Dave Goelz, Jerry Nelson, Richard Hunt, Steve Whitmire, Liza Minnelli. When the Muppets’ college revue is a big hit, they decide to take the show all the way to Broadway. Adjusting to the hustle and bustle of New York City, Kermit takes a job at a local restaurant while he searches for a producer. Filled with cameos by quintessential New Yorkers, such as Gregory Hines, Joan Rivers, James Coco, Brooke Shields, and Liza Minnelli, the movie ends with a fantastical and questionably genuine wedding between Kermit and Miss Piggy. Oz’s first solo-directed film is a dose of pure joy, a true gift to showtune lovers featuring some of the greatest songs in the Muppet canon and the beloved “Muppet Babies” sequence that spawned its own mini-franchise. Rated: G Preceded by: The Muppet Show Episode 414: Starring Liza Minnelli 1979, 23 mins. Liza Minnelli brought her many talents to The Muppet Show in its fourth season in 1979. In one of the handful of episodes that broke the show’s regular variety format, Liza headlines a Muppet murder mystery as an actress who hires private eye Kermit to solve a backstage crime—her show at the Roxy has been threatened by an anonymous culprit. In between the intrigue and dead bodies that keep turning up, Liza manages to deliver some top-notch musical numbers. Can Liza and Kermit solve the crime before the villain runs out of victims? screenings.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
screenings.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Side Street
screenings.description: Dir. Anthony Mann. 1949, 83 mins. 35mm. With Farley Granger, Cathy O’Donnell, James Craig. A part-time letter carrier foolishly steals $30,000 from gangsters and is soon on the run from them and the police. Mann returned to the city of his youth to direct this shattering film noir that reunites Granger with They Live by Night co-star Cathy O’Donnell. Following in the post-World War II tradition of such semi-documentary thrillers as The Naked City, Side Street makes spectacular use of New York locations as the tortured protagonist wanders everywhere from Midtown to Greenwich Village, from South Street Seaport to skid row, culminating in a gripping (and symbolic) car chase through the financial district. screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 2
screenings.description: “These three films, among Nelson’s most beautifully crafted works, were made during return trips to her home country, leading up to her move back to Sweden in 1993 after teaching for more than two decades at the San Francisco Art Institute. Frame Line blends still photographs (some of which she paints on) and moving images, showing the full range of her artistry as she revisits her past. Red Shift, filmed at her parents’ home in Kristinehamn, is a unique hybrid film with scripted and documentary elements, with Nelson, her daughter Oona, and her mother as ‘performers,’ punctuated by readings of letters from Calamity Jane to her daughter. Old Digs weaves together a murmuring soundtrack of a family gathering with roaming color images of a rustic village, layered with cut-out images added through stop-motion animation.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: Dinner With Friends + Q&A
screenings.description: After the parties, jobs, and hook-ups throughout their twenties and into their thirties, eight friends are trying to hold on to their group as they get older and life gets complicated. Over a series of dinners, the group deals with loyalty, loss, and an uncertain future as relationships shift and secrets are unraveled, with each dinner bringing its own dynamic shifting announcement of reconciliation, unexpected relationships, and betrayal. The city is crumbling, the climate is changing, and worries about the future of the world are making it hard for this group of friends to stay together. But they’ll come to realize everything would be much harder if they don’t.

screenings.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
screenings.description: Dir. Mehrdad Oskouei & Soraya. 2025, 96 mins. Iran, Turkey, Greece. DCP. In Farsi with English subtitles. A moving, artful, and surprising collaboration between the legendary Iranian filmmaker Mehrdad Oskouei and a whip-smart teenage artist, A Fox Under a Pink Moon follows Afghani refugee Soraya’s relentless efforts to escape an abusive marriage in Tehran and join her mother in Austria. But rather than the cliché frame of master and muse, Oskouei remotely directed Soraya to tell her own story, from both her reality and her imagination. In addition to many attempts to cross the border into Europe, Soraya escapes and resists oppression through her dark and unfettered artwork, which often features an enigmatic fox and weeping clown. It is her work that gives the film its shape and aching intimacy, from the watercolor animations derived from her drawings, to her smartphone video diaries tracking five years of survival separated from her home and loving family. Poetic and raw, A Fox Under a Pink Moon is as electric and courageous as its heroine, making it easy to see why this film won awards all over the world and is in serious discussion for the 2027 Oscars Awards. screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 3
screenings.description: "“Gunvor Nelson’s experience as a painter before becoming a filmmaker is at its most evident in these strikingly graphic films, all of which involve hands-on manipulation of the surfaces and textures of still and moving images. Light Years and Light Years Expanding use collage techniques while traversing the Swedish landscape, by train in the former and car in the latter. The final two works are made entirely in the studio. Nelson describes Natural Features as ‘a free associative and playfully bizarre form of animation. Here I used mirrors, water, toys, cut-outs, photographs, paint, ink … in many different combinations. The central theme is face.’ Experimenting with video, Nelson performs magic in Trace Elements, creating a visual dance between her camera and her shadow.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: That Day, On The Beach
screenings.description: The little-screened debut feature by Yang, prophet of and proselytizer for the Taiwanese New Wave, features Sylvia Chang and Terry Hu as two female friends, an unhappily married housewife and a concert pianist, brought together after a 13-year separation: their process of catching up illustrated through an innovative, ingeniously layered flashback structure which shows the director’s air for formal experimentation already fully in operation. Shot by renegade cinematographer Christopher Doyle, also on his first feature, Yang’s gorgeous and deeply felt memory piece/mystery uses its intricate structure to explore, among other things, “the ways in which patriarchal authority stunts young people’s lives.” US theatrical premiere of new 2K restoration.

screenings.title: Gigi
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1958, 115 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Leslie Caron, Louis Jourdan, Maurice Chevalier, Hermione Gingold. The CinemaScope frame is crammed with exquisite detail in this thrillingly visualized musical adapted from a story by Collette about a girl’s coming-of-age in wealthy turn-of-the-century Paris. Minnelli’s film is both tender and sly, a social satire of sexual mores as well as a moving tale of an innocent’s entrance into a complicated world in which women’s options are limited. The winner of nine Oscars (a record at the time), including Best Picture, Director, Cinematography, Art Direction, Costume Design, Song, and Score (by My Fair Lady composers Lerner and Loewe), Gigi is a triumph on every level, like a Toulouse-Lautrec painting sprung to giddy life. screenings.title: Emperor of the North
screenings.description: Inspired by the writings of legendary hobo Leon Ray Livingston, under the pen name “A-No.1,” Aldrich’s tale of the risks run rail-riding in the ’30s northwest stars Lee Marvin as top tramp A-No.1, locked in a battle royale struggle with Ernest Borgnine’s fascistic, hobo-hatin’ conductor Shack on the speeding #19 of the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railroad, while Keith Carradine’s rascally fellow stowaway looks on. Featuring gorgeous location photography, suicidal stuntwork on speeding period locomotives, and bone-breaking action, Emperor of the North is Aldrich at his brutal best.

screenings.title: Memento
screenings.description: The indie sensation that put a young English director named Christopher Nolan on the map for good, this strikingly original, ornately structured neo-noir stars Guy Pearce as Leonard, a man on a mission of revenge after a savage attack that left his wife dead and him with anterograde amnesia, unable to store new short-term memory and forced to rely on an elaborate note-taking system in order to continue his single-minded pursuit of justice. “A brilliant feat of rug-pulling… [Nolan is] clearly excited by the way the medium can manipulate time and information, folding straightforward events and simple motives into Möbius strips of paradox and indeterminacy… Like an existential crossword puzzle, or a pungent 50’s B-thriller with a script by Jorge Luis Borges.” —The New York Times

Impassioned performances by both leads make Sibyl a compelling study in obsession and self-delusion, with the added inducement of Anatomy star Sandra Hüller’s appearance in a side-splitting role as the director of a film-within-the-film.

screenings.title: Maîtres Anciens – Comédie
screenings.description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseillePreceded by:Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. With Barbara Hannigan.)“In C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE, I explore a mystery that fascinates me: where do these inhuman voices come from? From where in the body does the unsettling anomaly of singing originate?” –Mathieu AmalricTotal running time: ca. 100 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Orfeo
screenings.description: In the classic Greek tragedy, a snake bites Eurydice on her wedding day, and her new husband, Orpheus, travels to the Underworld to bring her back. Virgilio Villoresi’s expressionistic adaptation of the tale is based on Dino Buzzati’s 1969 Poema a fumetti, Italy ‘s first graphic novel. The film is a modern reimagining with an aesthetic untethered from reality: a kaleidoscopic journey through time and place, reflecting on art, love, mystery, eroticism, melancholy, life, and death.

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall in 35mm
screenings.description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. He reminds us about the painful past, explains the present, and warns about the future. His dramatic plea, "do not be indifferent!" remains more relevant now than ever. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: Wendy Carlos’s score of switched-on Moog synthesizer classical, Kubrick’s punchy framings, and Malcolm McDowell’s cruelly charismatic, Nadsat slang-spouting performance as teen reprobate Alex combine to make for cracking cinema, and a hallucinatory imagination of a future broken Britain. Based on the stinging satire by Anthony Burgess, a work by turns exhilarating and nauseating, the film of A Clockwork Orange would be withdrawn from British cinemas at Kubrick’s behest, citing concern over reports that it had inspired copycat crimes in the UK.

screenings.title: Somewhere in the Night
screenings.description: Mankiewicz’s sophomore effort as director was this sinisterly atmospheric, baroquely plotted, deliriously disorienting “nervous nightmare” [The Village Voice] starring John Hodiak as an amnesiac ex-Marine who returns to his native Los Angeles to trawl its nightclubs, sanitariums, and docks in search of clues to his identity and traces of a mysterious stranger by the name of “Larry Cravat.” It’s a mission that puts him in close contact with the criminal underworld and a rogue’s gallery of unusual characters (Richard Conte, Josephine Hutchinson, and Fritz Kortner are on-hand in piquant supporting parts) while tying him up in a hunt for Nazi-plundered treasure.

screenings.title: Mean Streets + Q&A
screenings.description: Just a Shot Away chronicles the brilliant and tumultuous life and career of Martin Scorsese, one of the world’s foremost living filmmakers, from his childhood on the violent streets of mid-century Little Italy, recreated in unprecedented detail, to his tectonic contributions to the cinema of the New Hollywood and beyond. The making of such masterpieces as Taxi Driver, Raging Bull, and The Last Waltz are explored here in revelatory depth, along with undersung favorites like Alice Doesn’t Live Here Anymore and After Hours.

screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

screenings.title: Barbara
screenings.description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin.Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: In Wim Wenders’ iconic Wings of Desire, two angels, Damiel and Cassiel, glide through the streets of a divided Berlin, observing the bustling population. When Damiel falls in love with lonely trapeze artist Marion, the angel longs to experience life in the physical world. Featuring a showstopping performance by a young Nick Cave, crooning the title track from From Her to Eternity, Wings of Desire is one of the most inexhaustible modern films.

Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. He reminds us about the painful past, explains the present, and warns about the future. His dramatic plea, "do not be indifferent!" remains more relevant now than ever. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

screenings.title: Portraits of the Artist
screenings.image: https://anthologyfilmarchives.org/uploads/Ludwig Schönherr - Portraitfilm Elisabeth Erkner - 3 © Arsenal Filminstitut copy.jpg
screenings.description: Beginning with Gerard Malanga’s ANDY WARHOL (1964), in which the author of the SCREEN TESTS sits for his own extended portrait, this program finds the directors turning the camera on their fellow filmmakers, or even trading places for complementary films (as in the case of the Friedl vom Gröller and Christiana Perschon films that close the screening).Gerard Malanga ANDY WARHOL: PORTRAITS OF THE ARTIST AS A YOUNG MAN (1964, 21 min, 16mm-to-DCP)Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: KURT KREN (1969, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent)Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: ELISABETH ERKNER (1969, 14 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent)Barry Gerson PORTRAIT OF ANDREW NOREN (1972, 4 min, 16mm, silent)Friedl vom Gröller I DON’T WANT TO BE FILMED BUT RATHER SHOOT MYSELF / ICH WILL NICHT GEFILMT WERDEN, SONDERN SELBER FILMEN (2023, 3 min, 16mm, silent)Christiana Perschon FRIEDL (2023, 2.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP)Friedl vom Gröller FLO UND KEN JACOBS (2001, 3 min, 16mm, silent)Friedl vom Gröller PETER KUBELKA UND JONAS MEKAS (1994, 2.5 min, 16mm, silent)Jeff Weber PETER (2026, 5.5 min, 35mm, silent)Total running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: Mr. Marian Turski, the world-renowned historian, journalist, and until his recent passing, president of the International Auschwitz Committee, takes us back to the roots of evil. A survivor of the Lodz Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Theresienstadt death camps in his youth, Turski explains with firsthand knowledge and surgical precision how otherwise well-educated and cultured people can, under certain circumstances, turn into criminals and mass murderers. He reminds us about the painful past, explains the present, and warns about the future. His dramatic plea, "do not be indifferent!" remains more relevant now than ever. Andrzej Wolf, the director and cinematographer of this film, pays a loving tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation.

screenings.description: Starring Tim Curry Susan Sarandon Barry Bostwick Richard O'Brien Patricia Quinn Little Nell Meat Loaf

screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: The Aristocats
screenings.description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from the accustomed baronial splendor of their home, have to rely on the streetwise wiles of alley cat O’Malley to keep them safe. Featuring animation supremely attentive to the syntax of kitty motion and the vocal talents of Eva Gabor and Scatman Crothers who gets to lead on the boppin' classic “Everybody Wants to Be a Cat.”

screenings.title: A Man Walks Down the Street
screenings.description: Raanan, a middle aged man, returns home after 30 years abroad. A chance encounter with an elderly man unlocks troubled memories, and a brief affair with a much younger man, send him spiraling through generational rifts, and force him to confront his internalized homophobia and emotional wounds of his past.

screenings.title: The General
screenings.description: Keaton’s engineer Johnnie Gray is another of his big-hearted little guys, rejected by the Confederate Army, though when the Union tries to make off with his train, runt Johnnie shows his mettle in the most incredible sustained chase sequence in all of silent comedy. Wall-to-wall with elaborate, antic gags, though also marked by a quiet sense of pastoral beauty that had previously been given little outlet.

screenings.title: The Muppet Christmas Carol: The Uncut Version
screenings.description: Dir. Brian Henson. 1992, 85 mins. U.S. DCP. With Michael Caine, Dave Goelz, Steve Whitmire, Jerry Nelson, Frank Oz. In this beloved staple of many a childhood, the Charles Dickens classic is recast with the classic Muppet characters, including Gonzo as Charles Dickens, Kermit at Bob Cratchit, and Fozzie Bear as Fozziwig. This faithful adaptation is as full of Christmas spirit and imagination as any of the various film adaptations of the novel, and features a towering performance by Caine as the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge and a splendid musical score by Paul Williams. This full, uncut version of the original release features the song “When Love Is Gone.” Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. screenings.title: The Sacrifice
screenings.description: Made when Tarkovsky was already suffering greatly from the lung cancer that would end his life, his last film is one of cinema’s greatest final testaments, a work that puts both pagan and Christian traditions of self-sacrifice into dialectic conversation. Shot in Sweden with renowned cinematographer Sven Nykvist and featuring several other Ingmar Bergman collaborators, including actor Erland Josephson, the gorgeous and deeply affecting film, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, takes place at a birthday gathering that’s interrupted by news warning of an imminent nuclear holocaust.

screenings.title: Secrets & Lies
screenings.description: The winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1996 Cannes Film Festival, Leigh’s tender, funny, fearless film has Brenda Blethyn in a career-best performance as Cynthia, a white working-class woman who has a life-changing revelation when she meets Black middle-class optometrist Marianne Jean-Baptiste, who informs Cynthia she’s the little girl Cynthia had given up for adoption 27 years ago, all grown up. Developed, like all of Leigh’s films, through a process of collaborative improvisation, it’s a film of startling spontaneity and uncomfortable, unflinching emotional honesty.

screenings.title: Bells Are Ringing
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1960, 126 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Judy Holliday, Dean Martin, Fred Clark, Jean Stapleton. In his delightful musical pairing with Oscar-winner Judy Holliday and superstar Dean Martin, Minnelli directs an effervescent New York–set romantic comedy about a nosy Brooklyn telephone operator for an answering service who finds herself falling for a poor wannabe playwright while also trying to play matchmaker to her other clients. With her tender, metropolitan vivaciousness, Holliday is as note-perfect as always, while the film is also a showcase for the musical talents of composers Betty Comden and Adolph Green, from whose Broadway hit the show is adapted. Bells Are Ringing would be the final musical from the famed MGM Freed Unit, and earned Minnelli a DGA nomination for Best Director. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Rashomon
screenings.description: A riveting psychological thriller and arthouse sensation starring Toshiro Mifune and Machiko Kyō which investigates the nature of truth and the meaning of justice, widely considered one of the key texts of Japanese—and world—cinema. Four people give different accounts of a man’s murder and the rape of his wife, which Kurosawa presents with striking imagery (those shafts of sunlight streaming through the forest canopy!) and ingenious use of flashbacks. Shooting the celebrated opening of his film—a torrential downfall at Rashomon Gate—Kurosawa and crew mixed water with black ink in the rain tank, creating one of the most sinister soaks in cinema history.

screenings.title: Medea (1988)
screenings.description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish cinema making himself a medium for the Old Master’s vision, setting the source material in a pre-Christian Denmark. “An experimental film in the true sense of the word… Taking the greatest limitation of video—the medium’s lack of depth of field—Mr. von Trier turns it into a strength, flattening perspectives in a way that collapses his foreground characters into the tumultuous backgrounds (waves, wind-swept fields) that surround and dominate them.” —Dave Kehr, The New York Times

screenings.title: Mean Streets
screenings.description: In New York City’s Little Italy, a devoutly Catholic mobster must reconcile his desire for power, his feelings for his epileptic girlfriend, and his devotion to his troublesome friend.

screenings.title: Columbus
screenings.description: Modern architecture acts as a vehicle for emotional expression in Kogonada’s lauded first feature, whose title refers to the Indiana city that, thanks to the patronage of Cummins diesel engines company cofounder J. Irwin Miller, has commissioned buildings from master builders including I.M. Pei, Eero Saarinen, and Robert Venturi. A Korean American translator (John Cho) arrives in this curious testing ground for advanced architecture after his estranged scholar father falls ill, there to cross paths with dad’s protégée (Parker Posey), an aesthete clerk at the local library (Haley Lu Richardson), and a bevy of singular structures. A film of rich colors and muted yearning, and one of the most distinctive debuts in the last decade of American independent cinema.

screenings.title: The Best Secret Agent
screenings.description: The movie that lit the fuse on an explosion of espionage thrillers in Taiwan, Zhang’s box-office phenomenon is a twisty tale of star-crossed love and sabotage during the years of the Sino-Japanese war, featuring Bai Hong as a refugee from the marauding Japanese who land in Shanghai, Ke Junxiong as the man she falls for, and Tian Qing as the collaborationist stooge of the puppet Manchukuo state that she reluctantly marries—his schemes constantly undermined by the actions of a mysterious “Secret Agent Heaven No. 1.” A spry, stylish, sexy cloak-and-dagger melodrama, based on a homonymous 1945 film from the Mainland, with Hong a delight as she dons several walk-in closets’ worth of disguises.

screenings.title: Screen Tests + Screen Tests Revisited, Pgm 1
The Fin + Q&A
screenings.description: In a post-war and ecologically devastated Korea, mutated outcasts called Omegas are exploited as cheap labor. Sujin, a young government worker, begins to doubt the state’s ideology as she pursues Mia, an Omega in hiding.

screenings.title: A Man Walks Down the Street

A chance encounter with an elderly man unlocks troubled memories, and a brief affair with a much younger man, send him spiraling through generational rifts, and force him to confront his internalized homophobia and emotional wounds of his past.

screenings.title: Taxi Driver
screenings.description: “Suck on this!” A pure distillation of needling isolation, inadequacy, and anguish, all roiling in the tortured gut of Robert De Niro’s insomniac cabbie Travis Bickle, who cruises all night through a stygian, steam-choked Manhattan, nursing his fears and hatreds. A defining picture of New York City in 1976, and a movie that is wrenched straight from the unquiet psyche of its screenwriter, exorcizing his personal demons.

screenings.title: Compartment No. 6
screenings.description: When her girlfriend bails on a planned trip to visit ancient petroglyphs in the remote city of Murmansk in the Arctic Circle, Finnish student Laura (Seidi Haarla) decides to go on alone, finding herself sharing a compartment on the long train from Moscow with Lyokha (Yura Borisov), a Russian returning to his work in the mines of the northeast who makes a belligerent and boorish first impression, but in time becomes a figure of fascination for Laura—and she for him.

screenings.title: Screen Tests + Screen Tests Revisited, Pgm 2
Wings of Desire
screenings.description: In Wim Wenders’ iconic Wings of Desire, two angels, Damiel and Cassiel, glide through the streets of a divided Berlin, observing the bustling population. When Damiel falls in love with lonely trapeze artist Marion, the angel longs to experience life in the physical world. Featuring a showstopping performance by a young Nick Cave, crooning the title track from From Her to Eternity, Wings of Desire is one of the most inexhaustible modern films.
screenings.country: Wings of Desire Drama, Fantasy, Romance

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: Wendy Carlos’s score of switched-on Moog synthesizer classical, Kubrick’s punchy framings, and Malcolm McDowell’s cruelly charismatic, Nadsat slang-spouting performance as teen reprobate Alex combine to make for cracking cinema, and a hallucinatory imagination of a future broken Britain. Based on the stinging satire by Anthony Burgess, a work by turns exhilarating and nauseating, the film of A Clockwork Orange would be withdrawn from British cinemas at Kubrick’s behest, citing concern over reports that it had inspired copycat crimes in the UK.

screenings.title: Mandy
screenings.description: After Nicolas Cage’s pacific, reclusive life with his girlfriend Mandy is interrupted by the arrival of members of an apocalyptic cannibalistic cult, the Children of the New Dawn, he’ll have to pay a visit to his old pal, Caruthers (Duke), to pick up his trusty crossbow, sights set on revenge. Duke provides a moment of authority and gravity, just before this strikingly styled early ‘80s-set instant cult classic plunges into madness courtesy of Cage at his most frantic, feral, and fatally fierce.

screenings.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
screenings.description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King Hu’s 1967 wuxia epic Dragon Inn, playing to a motley smattering of spectators, including two stars of Hu’s original opus, Miao Tien and Shih Chun, watching their younger selves with tears in their eyes.

screenings.title: A Separation
screenings.description: Farhadi combines elements of the domestic drama and psychological thriller in his trenchant, lacerating 2012 Academy Award winner for Best Foreign Film. Simin (Leila Hatami) wants to emigrate with her 11-year-old daughter and with or without her husband, Nader (Payman Maadi), who, with the support of the court, has dug in his heels to keep the family in place while he looks after his ailing father, aided by a caregiver with costly secrets. Through the intersecting stories of two deadlocked couples—one middle-class, the other working-class—and their necessary deceptions, Farhadi shows us a microcosm of contemporary Iranian society and the insoluble moral dilemmas it presents to ordinary men and women.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Emperor of the North
screenings.description: Inspired by the writings of legendary hobo Leon Ray Livingston, under the pen name “A-No.1,” Aldrich’s tale of the risks run rail-riding in the ’30s northwest stars Lee Marvin as top tramp A-No.1, locked in a battle royale struggle with Ernest Borgnine’s fascistic, hobo-hatin’ conductor Shack on the speeding #19 of the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railroad, while Keith Carradine’s rascally fellow stowaway looks on. Featuring gorgeous location photography, suicidal stuntwork on speeding period locomotives, and bone-breaking action, Emperor of the North is Aldrich at his brutal best.

screenings.title: Railway Sleepers preceded by A Child Already Knows
screenings.description: Shot over the course of eight years on every line and spur of Thailand’s rail system, its mountains of footage culled down to appear as one 48-hour journey, Chidgasornpongse’s Apichatpong Weerasethakul–produced documentary is both a mesmeric travelogue and a portrait of a country and a people in flux. Screens with A Child Already Knows, in which Sia, employing Mao-era kid’s cartoons and other archival morsels, recounts her family’s flight from Shanghai to Hong Kong.

screenings.title: The Manchurian Candidate
screenings.description: The 1960 U-2 incident, and rumors of the brainwashing of downed Air Force pilot Francis Gary Powers by Soviet captors, were fresh in the imagination when Frankenheimer’s taut political suspenser hit screens, featuring Laurence Harvey as Raymond Shaw, a Korean War vet returned stateside with decorations after going MIA—unbeknownst to himself and the wider world, a sleeper agent programmed to do the bidding of the Commies—and Frank Sinatra the Army Intelligence officer who suspects all might not be right with Sgt. Shaw. “One of the strangest and most mercurial movies ever made in Hollywood… Conceivably the only commercial American film that deserves to be linked with the French New Wave, full of visual and verbal wit that recalls Orson Welles… A powerful experience, alternately corrosive with dark parodic humor, suspenseful, moving, and terrifying.” —Jonathan Rosenbaum, The Chicago Reader

screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The brainchild of provocateur extraordinaires Paul Verhoeven and Joe Eszterhas, Basic Instinct was one of the most controversial films of the 90s (protested by LGBTQ activists for its portrayal of the film’s bisexual femme fatale) and a runaway box office smash. When detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas) becomes ensnared in a web of sex, lies, and violence, all the evidence points to Catherine Tramell (Sharon Stone, in a star-making role), a seductive, mysterious crime novelist. As the bodies pile up and hidden obsessions are revealed, Curran begins to doubt his investigatory instincts and give in to his baser ones.

screenings.title: Hannah and Her Sisters
screenings.description: Between three Thanksgivings two years apart, Hannah’s husband falls in love with her sister Lee, while her hypochondriac ex-husband rekindles his relationship with her sister Holly.

Although Richard Abel has astutely called attention to aspects the film shares with Abel Gance’s LA ROUE (1923) and Leon Moussinac’s LE BRASIER ARDENT (1923)…and with Jean Epstein’s COEUR FIDELE (1923)…any comparison of the film as a whole with those admirable works would have to underline the intensity, uniqueness, and exceptional rigor of Kirsanoff’s achievement.” –P. screenings.title: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
screenings.description: Pasolini’s final film remains one of the most shocking ever made. Set during a waning fascist Italy’s dark days amidst World War II, Salò updates the writings of Marquis de Sade to create a repugnant tale of four wealthy libertines who kidnap a group of teenage boys and girls and enact horrific humiliations and violence upon them. A formally and conceptually brilliant, if relentlessly nauseating, portrayal of man’s most debased instincts and the capitalist systems that allow them to thrive. Per Pasolini, “The most sincere thing I could do at that moment was to make a film about a mode of sexuality whose joyousness is a compensation for repression—a phenomenon that was about to come to an end, forever.”

screenings.title: Six Suspects
screenings.description: Keeping an eye on his ex-lover (Zhang Qingqing), the personal assistant to the chairman of a large steel company, private eye Kong-hui (Wu Dongru) picks up ample fodder to blackmail the folks in the front office—and so, when Kong-hui is found murdered, detective Yi Yuan won’t lack for suspects… though each trail he follows seems to lead to a dead end. A jazzy, ingeniously plotted urban whodunnit set in a Taipei in the first flush of postwar prosperity, Six Suspects was not granted a theatrical release on completion but has now been revealed, thanks to restoration work by the Taiwan Film Institute, as a darkly glittering gem of the mid-century Taiyupian.

screenings.title: Another Day in Paradise with Larry Clark
screenings.description: In the hope of a big score, two junkie couples team up to commit various drug robberies which go disastrously wrong, leading to dissent, violence, and murder.
screenings.country: MM with Larry Clark Crime, Drama, Thriller, Comedy

This sophisticated and grotesque screen farce – eloquently touching, uproariously hilarious – is a perfect example of Keaton’s art. Engulfed by switches, stolen engines, valves, and other mechanical contrivances, the immortal comedian – an engine driver literally on the wrong side of the tracks – solemnly attempts to behave normally in a world which is plainly bewitched.” –CINEMA 16 program notes, 1958Preceded by:Buster Keaton & Edward F. Cline NEIGHBORS (1920, 18 min, 16mm, silent)CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Film No. 5 (smile)
screenings.description: “[S]hot with a high-speed camera…FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) reveals John Lennon’s face, recorded at 333 frames per second for an extended duration, outdoors, in color, and accompanied by a sound track of outdoor sounds recorded at the same time the imagery was recorded. FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) divides roughly into two halves, one continuous shot each. During the first half, the film is a meditation on Lennon’s face, which is so still that on first viewing I wasn’t entirely sure for a while that the film was live action and not an optically printed photograph of Lennon smiling slightly. Though almost nothing happens in any conventional sense, however, the intersection of the high speed filming and our extended gaze creates continuous, subtle transformations. […] While the second shot is more active than the first, the amount of activity remains minimal by conventional standards (and unusually so even for avant-garde film). It is as though those of us in the theater and Lennon are meditating on each other from opposite sides of the cinematic apparatus, joined together by Ono in a lovely, hypnotic stasis.” –Scott MacDonald, “Yoko Ono: Ideas on Film”Preceded by:Yoko OnoFLUXFILM NO. 16: aka NO. 4: BOTTOMS1966, 6 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent. Camera: Jeff Perkins, Anthony Cox. Starring: Susannah Campbell, Philip Corner, Anthony Cox, Bici Hendricks, Geoffrey Hendricks, Kyoko Ono, Yoko Ono, Ben Patterson, Jeff Perkins, Susan Poland, Jerry Sablo, Carolee Schneemann, James Tenney, Pieter Vanderbeck, Verne Williams.“The rebellious, erotic, liberatory nature of the film, which reflects the tenor of Fluxus, acts in direct opposition to the nineteenth-century scientific treatment of the body as a ‘dynamic field of action in need of regulation and control.’” –Chrissie Iles, “Erotic Conceptualism: The Films of Yoko Ono”Total running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Memento
screenings.description: The indie sensation that put a young English director named Christopher Nolan on the map for good, this strikingly original, ornately structured neo-noir stars Guy Pearce as Leonard, a man on a mission of revenge after a savage attack that left his wife dead and him with anterograde amnesia, unable to store new short-term memory and forced to rely on an elaborate note-taking system in order to continue his single-minded pursuit of justice. “A brilliant feat of rug-pulling… [Nolan is] clearly excited by the way the medium can manipulate time and information, folding straightforward events and simple motives into Möbius strips of paradox and indeterminacy… Like an existential crossword puzzle, or a pungent 50’s B-thriller with a script by Jorge Luis Borges.” —The New York Times

screenings.title: Jump Scare
screenings.description: An all-female metal band called “Jump Scare” retreats to a remote cabin to write their next album, only to be terrorized by the family of cannibals next door. The film is part phantasmagoric homage to filmmakers like Don Coscarelli and Chuck Russell, part punk-rock ode to grindhouse slasher cinema, and a post-modern cannibal film that also happens to co-star everyone’s favorite working actor, Eric Roberts.

screenings.title: Millennium Mambo
screenings.description: A stylish and seductive submersion into the techno-scored neon nightlife of Taipei, Hou’s much-misunderstood marvel stars Shu Qi (The Assassin) as an aimless bar hostess drifting away from her blowhard boyfriend and towards Jack Kao’s suave, sensitive gangster. Structured as a flashback to the then-present from the then-future of 2011, it’s a transfixing trance-out of a movie, drenched in club lights, ecstatic endorphin-rush exhilaration, and a nagging undercurrent of ennui. Hou and longtime cinematographer Lee here break from their familiar pattern of elegantly composed long shot long takes to create something both more intimate and hectic, a film whose shallow-focus images, jittery camerawork, and cramped locations evoke both the claustrophobic character of Taiwan’s capital city and, in Lee’s words, “the feeling of youth.”

screenings.title: Suspiria [4K DCP]
screenings.description: A fairy tale construction at once grim and florid, Argento’s best-known film finds Jessica Harper’s American ballet dancer arriving at an exclusive academy in Germany where she discovers a dark past and occult forces at work in the present. With some of Argento’s most perversely ingenious set pieces, a plum part for former Fritz Lang muse Joan Bennett, and a spine-tingling theme by Goblin that will haunt you to the grave.

screenings.title: The Ascent
screenings.description: The bloodthirsty and seemingly unstoppable Nazi war machine is on the march towards Moscow in Shepitko’s wrenching, snow-swept World War II drama, which begins with two Soviet peasant soldiers foraging for food in a Belarusian village and proceeds to tell an emotional, lyrical tale of loyalty and betrayal, partisanship and collaboration, and, ultimately, the possibility of transcendent redemption. Shepitko’s final feature, frequently cited as among the greatest of Soviet films, won the Golden Bear at the 1977 Berlin Film Festival, just two years before its director’s tragic death in a car accident at age 41.

screenings.title: The Rescuers
screenings.description: Geraldine Page, Bob Newhart, and Eva Gabor are among the vocal talent assembled for Disney’s vivacious adaptation of Margery Sharp’s beloved book series about the Rescue Aid Society, a group of dauntless mice who travel the world to lend aid to kidnapping victims. Here R.A.S. representatives Miss Bianca (Gabor) and Bernard (Newhart) rush to Devil’s Bayou, Louisiana, where they liberate a little girl named Penny from the clutches of the nefarious Madame Medusa (Page) and her trained crocodiles, Brutus and Nero, while at the same time tasked with keeping a precious gemstone safe from the villainess. A spirited, swashbuckling adventure, made with brio by Disney’s crack animation team led by rising star Don Bluth.

screenings.title: Once Upon A Time In The West
screenings.description: "Along with dream team collaborators Leone and Bernardo Bertolucci, Dario Argento is credited with the story for this epic oater, a sort of link between the established Spaghetti Western and the rising giallo, both genres defined by their elaborate and sometimes insanely involved set pieces. Honest Henry Fonda goes bad—very bad—as a railroad baron’s hired gun, facing off against Bronson’s lethal loner Harmonica, in the soaring, musically composed movie that really earns the label of “horse opera.”

screenings.title: The Manchurian Candidate
screenings.description: The 1960 U-2 incident, and rumors of the brainwashing of downed Air Force pilot Francis Gary Powers by Soviet captors, were fresh in the imagination when Frankenheimer’s taut political suspenser hit screens, featuring Laurence Harvey as Raymond Shaw, a Korean War vet returned stateside with decorations after going MIA—unbeknownst to himself and the wider world, a sleeper agent programmed to do the bidding of the Commies—and Frank Sinatra the Army Intelligence officer who suspects all might not be right with Sgt. Shaw. “One of the strangest and most mercurial movies ever made in Hollywood… Conceivably the only commercial American film that deserves to be linked with the French New Wave, full of visual and verbal wit that recalls Orson Welles… A powerful experience, alternately corrosive with dark parodic humor, suspenseful, moving, and terrifying.” —Jonathan Rosenbaum, The Chicago Reader

screenings.title: Barbara Forever + Q&A
screenings.description: BARBARA FOREVER is an expansive, immersive exploration of the life, work, and ongoing cultural impact of filmmaker Barbara Hammer – a pioneering artist who lived boldly, created urgently, and transformed cinema through her singular vision. Her films were an extension of herself: sensual, experimental, and unapologetically lesbian, rooted in a profound desire for connection and an insistence on telling her own story. Driven by her canon of over eighty films, a vast collection of unreleased archival materials, and extensive audio interviews, Brydie O’Connor’s portrait allows for Hammer’s voice and images to shine through, becoming both a tribute and an extension of her legacy.

screenings.title: The Piano

screenings.description: The third and final Dragon Superman adventure opens with a pack of masked baddies kidnapping two children in a Japanese garden, a high-kicking, bone-cracking donnybrook, and some sinister plotting involving a “mummy drug” and “invisibility experiments”… and that’s just the first five minutes! A defining picture of New York City in 1976, and a movie that is wrenched straight from the unquiet psyche of its screenwriter, exorcizing his personal demons.

screenings.title: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
screenings.description: Pasolini’s final film remains one of the most shocking ever made. Set during a waning fascist Italy’s dark days amidst World War II, Salò updates the writings of Marquis de Sade to create a repugnant tale of four wealthy libertines who kidnap a group of teenage boys and girls and enact horrific humiliations and violence upon them. A formally and conceptually brilliant, if relentlessly nauseating, portrayal of man’s most debased instincts and the capitalist systems that allow them to thrive. Per Pasolini, “The most sincere thing I could do at that moment was to make a film about a mode of sexuality whose joyousness is a compensation for repression—a phenomenon that was about to come to an end, forever.”

screenings.title: Galaxie
screenings.description: A pinnacle of the art of filmic portraiture, Gregory Markopoulos’s GALAXIE comprises thirty short portraits of men and women from across the spectrum of the mid-1960s cultural scene in New York City. Its subjects include many of Markopoulos’s fellow experimental filmmakers – Storm De Hirsch, George & Mike Kuchar, Jonas Mekas, Shirley Clarke, Amy Taubin, and Ed Emshwiller – as well as figures from the literary and art worlds, including Parker Tyler, Jasper Johns, W.H. Auden, Allen Ginsberg, Kenneth Kelman, Maurice Sendak, Susan Sontag, and others. In keeping with Markopoulos’s short-form masterpieces MING GREEN, BLISS, and SORROWS, each of the individual portraits in GALAXIE was edited entirely in-camera, a near-miraculous feat given the intricate use of multiple layers of superimposition, all of it achieved by rewinding and making additional passes through the single 100-foot (ca. 3-minute) roll of 16mm film during the shoot. Initially intending to produce only a handful of portraits, Markopoulos ended up filming 40 different chapters, and ultimately incorporated the first 30 into the completed work (presented in the order they were created). Each of the portraits represents an exquisite visual record of the encounter between subject and filmmaker, while the film as a whole provides an extraordinary opportunity to observe the gradual development of Markopoulos’s approach to portraiture and in-camera editing.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: New Yorkers + Before the First Word
screenings.description: This program pairs two films, made a decade apart, that vividly demonstrate the vibrant, distinctive, and sometimes paradoxical nature of New York City’s neighborhoods: at once strikingly diverse and worldly, and yet close knit and self-enclosed. NEW YORKERS (1971), by filmmaker Michael Blackwood (who during his long career made several films about the city, as well as dozens of documentaries about artists, architects, and musicians), sets its sights on the Upper East Side, and in particular on the area in and around East 77th Street. BEFORE THE FIRST WORD (1982) – a co-production between WNET and the educational organization Learning Designs, and ostensibly a film designed as a teaching tool for journalism students – is set seventy-something blocks to the south, in Greenwich Village. screenings.title: Every Contact Leaves a Trace
screenings.description: “For most of her life, filmmaker Lynne Sachs has saved every business card ever placed into her hand – more than 600 fragments of chance encounters, fleeting conversations, and unexpected connections. Drawing on the forensic principle that every contact leaves a trace, Sachs selects seven cards and follows them back into the lives they represent. screenings.title: Love Letter
screenings.description: Pining for a love that is pained and futile, the young mistress of a well-known, married poet spends her days waiting for her lover to return in this subtle, slice-of-life drama made for Roman Porno’s 10th Anniversary. An unusual hit among female spectators.

screenings.title: Brighton Beach
screenings.description: At once a charming portrait of the diverse residents of a unique New York City neighborhood, a vibrant time capsule of the city at the very beginning of the 1980s, and a penetrating exploration of the social and political dynamics of a rapidly changing community, BRIGHTON BEACH is a long-lost gem of documentary cinema that has been newly restored by IndieCollect. Directed with great empathy and perceptiveness by Carol Stein & Susan Wittenberg, BRIGHTON BEACH captures the Brooklyn neighborhood known as the poor man’s paradise – a city by the sea down the street from the Coney Island boardwalk. Interspersing interviews with the neighborhood’s residents – including the Soviet Jews who had begun arriving in large numbers at the time – with archival footage of the area fifty years earlier, the film is both a portrait of a very particular time and place as well as a study of the ways in which urban communities function, cohere, and continuously transform themselves.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Angel Guts: Red Classroom
screenings.description: Overwrought with an exuding sense of melancholia in tone and exuberant mise-en-scène, Chusei Sone’s adroitly self-reflexive Red Classroom is a brooding, almost lyrical portrait of Takashi Ishii’s tragic figures of Muraki and Nami, buried in relentless traumas, desires and deep loneliness.

screenings.title: Drinking and Driving
screenings.description: Early twenties Iris (Jillian Frank) and Palmer (Avalon Fast) never left their hometown. They work at the same restaurant, share the same bed, and both have a habit of drinking and driving. They run into Levi (Ethan Hawksworth), a guy they used to know. They spend time with him and his cousin, Phoenix (Henri Gillespi), in cars, backyards, and other people’s bedrooms. When Levi shares a dream he had with Iris, things change between the four of them. The reality of the summer becomes faded, the parties die. The four end in a field of unified confusion.

screenings.title: 67 Bombs to Enid + Q&A
screenings.description: Between 1946 and 1958, the U.S. detonated 67 nuclear bombs in the Marshall Islands, contaminating the region and leaving generations of Marshallese facing illness. Decades later, many of the survivors and their descendants are building a new life in the United States.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Paradox on 72nd Street
screenings.description: Over the course of three years, Gene Searchinger filmed pedestrians, joggers, buskers, bench sitters, stoop sleepers, and countless other types of New Yorker (whom the narration describes as “exaggerated Americans”) at the corner of Broadway and 72nd St. Visually, the film presents an hour-long stream of individuals, each with their own unfathomable inner mindscape, who together comprise “the collective”; the paradox referred to in the title is narrator Lewis Thomas’s assertion that, “It is in our genes to live together and to depend on each other, to be our individual separate selves and at the same time the working parts of others.” Thomas, a biologist and the film’s co-writer, shares narrating duties with the anthropologist Philip Slater, both of whom offer meandering philosophical notes on individualism in American society.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Social Life of Small Urban Spaces
screenings.description: This film emerged from city planner William H. Whyte’s years of research into pedestrian behavior and city dynamics, conducted as part of his Street Life Project. His research resulted both in a film and a book, both of which closely analyzed the functioning of public spaces in various cities, above all in NYC. The book quickly became a classic text within the realm of city planning, and remains beloved not only for the wisdom and elegance of its insights, but for its disarmingly unpretentious, no-nonsense, and often flat-out funny tone. The film version fully embodies all the qualities of the book, and adds one special feature: Whyte’s own voice. Sounding very much like Jimmy Stewart’s city planner cousin, Whyte delivers the narration with an often-self-deprecatory folksiness that’s charmingly at odds with the stentorian tone of most educational films. The film is also effectively a work of street photography. Whyte and his team’s dedication to observing – and recording – the actual behavior of city dwellers, and their sharp eye for the behaviors and gestures that are most revealing of city life, result in a film that is – almost incidentally – a classic city symphony. THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES is one of the great films about that strangest of creatures – the city dweller – in its natural habitat.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Talk To Her
screenings.description: A travel writer’s burgeoning relationship with a famed female matador is violently interrupted when she falls into a coma after a bullring tragedy, and while waiting at her hospital bedside, he meets a male nurse keeping a similar vigil over a comatose ballet dancer. Only Almodóvar could come up with such a deliciously ridiculous premise for a film, and only Almodóvar could make it into a melodrama of unusual emotional power.

screenings.title: What Is the City but the People?
screenings.description: “In 1969 the Department of City Planning attempted to shore up support for its various [development] projects with a multipronged, multimedia public relations blitz. At its center was the publication of a six-volume book, ‘The Plan for New York City’ (1969), which articulated the commissioner’s vision for the metropolis to stem the flight of the middle classes to the suburbs and revitalize urban space. The plan was presented in synopsis form as a propagandistic documentary produced by the Department and co-directed by John Peer Nugent and Gordon Hyatt. Featuring some flashy cinematography from New York location shooter-extraordinaire Arthur J. Ornitz [THE CONNECTION; MINNIE & MOSKOWITZ; SERPICO], WHAT IS THE CITY is an idiosyncratic document of the city in the late 1960s, offering a wide panorama of places and spaces, narrated by one of the plan’s ghost writers, William H. Whyte [THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES]. The film flits between footage of and discussion about ‘urban crisis’ (uprisings, poor housing stock, street violence) and purported city-led remedies. Viewed today, the film is both a curious relic of failed urban policy and an index of just how wedded city authorities were (and remain) to the idea that the manipulation of public perception is key to urban governance.” –FILM AT LINCOLN CENTERCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Ghost World
screenings.description: The story of neo-cool Enid (Thora Birch) and Rebecca (Scarlett Johansson) who, faced with graduation from high school, take a hard look at the world they wryly observe and decide what they really want. When Enid takes an interest in the offbeat Seymour (Steve Buscemi) and Rebecca focuses her attention on their mutual romantic fixation Josh (Brad Renfro), the girls’ friendship is forever changed.

screenings.title: Cinexpérimentaux: a Meeting with Abigail Child
screenings.image: https://anthologyfilmarchives.org/uploads/Encounter_Child with The Future Is Behind You copy.jpg

screenings.title: Third Avenue: Only the Strong Survive
screenings.description: “This Emmy Award-winning documentary tells the stories of six ‘ordinary’ people who live or work along New York City’s Third Avenue, which runs for sixteen miles through Manhattan, Brooklyn, and the Bronx, cutting through the complex social strata of the city to reveal wildly different economic and ethnic subcultures. The subjects speak for themselves, offering candid glimpses into the disparate worlds of a junkyard dealer who steals cars, a Bowery denizen and the wife he abandoned, a welfare mother living in a condemned building with her five children, a sex worker, a devout Puerto Rican factory worker, and an aging Italian barber and his wife. This unsentimental portrait of the uncommon lives of common people is a subjective sociological study of survival in urban America.” –DCTVCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!
